We have a limited-time opportunity: Every dollar donated until September 30 will be matched 3X, thanks to a generous group of donors. | = To: Peter From: Tiernan Donohue, Chief Campaigns Officer Date: September 26, 2026 Subject: 38 Days Left — The Path to Taking Back Power ===================================================== At the start of 2025, we promised that we would put women at the center of the fight to take back power in this country, and with 38 days left, EMILYs List has delivered on that promise. Mission Majority: A Strategic Initiative That Puts EMILYs List Women At the Center of the Path to Flip the U.S. House Back in early 2025 when EMILYs laid out the most aggressive target map for the House of any national organization, a lot of people said it was too ambitious. Today, because of our recruitment work and candidate services, close to a dozen of those races are rated as "Toss Ups" and we have 25 Majority Makers running in the districts that we can flip and will decide control of the U.S. House. From top-tier battlegrounds to emerging seats where strong candidates and grassroots energy have put previously safe GOP-held seats into play. EMILYs List is fully mobilized behind these key races. Flipping the U.S. Senate: Our Candidates Are the Strategy In the battle for the Senate majority, EMILYs List women have made seats previously thought to be tough territory highly competitive. Our candidates are proving to be the strongest messengers on the issues that will decide this election — lowering the cost of living, expanding access to quality healthcare, and taking on corruption. These races are going to be at the center of the fight to flip the Senate heading into November. State Power Plan: Our Plan To Take Back Governing Power in Nine Key States We've seen states serve as a critical check against the chaos and cruelty coming out of Washington. To counter Republicans' partisan gerrymandering, preserve our healthcare, and enact policies that make life easier for everyday Americans, we need to build Democratic governing power in critical states this November. That's why EMILYs List recruited, launched, and trained strong candidates running up and down the ballot in nine key states: Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, New Mexico, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin. These are states where we can break Republican governing trifectas, elect women governors for the first time, and take back power at the state level heading into the crucial 2028 election. Our staff across the country are digging in on the data and reporting on increasing potential powered by voter enthusiasm and a real desire to see change. There are only 38 days left until Election Day. This is the window where investment translates most directly into votes — funding the final push of paid media and organizing programs that will decide these races on the margins. Make no mistake, these races will be close. body:
I’ve heard it over and over again from the political pundits this year

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140015119/649243516/-1547774912?refcode=email_092626_odds&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NTc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3Yjg4YTBmNC1iM2I5LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zbQRii3KulXylWbQF3kfcbx9Qn3gvxMXeFJp22E4Rs8=) I’ve heard it over and over again from the political pundits this year — and I’m sure you’ve heard the same: They’re saying these midterms are already decided. That Democrats won, National Republicans lost — and that the outcome is already set in stone. **But I don’t put a lot of stock into what the pundits have to say. About this election, or any other for that matter.** Because I remember what the pundits said about me: “There’s no way a former MMA fighter can win in Kansas.” “There’s no way an LGBTQ+ Native American woman can win _again_ in 2020.” “There’s no way she can overcome a gerrymandered district — new borders drawn specifically to take her down.” Frankly, I don’t care what the pundits say about this election. Because I am living proof of just how often they’re wrong. So I'm going to give this election 100%, everything I’ve got in the tank — just like I always have before. **And I need you to give 100% too — to chip in, support our campaign, and power this movement to victory — just like you always have.** [**We need to reach every voter we can before mail-in ballots go out early next month — and the only way we can do it is by hitting this critical FEC End-of-Quarter fundraising goal on Wednesday night. I mean it when I tell you the work we’re doing right now _matters_. I know there’s a lot of noise out there between the 24-hour news cycles, cable TV, social media, and of course this chaotic administration. But this work we’re doing together on the ground in Minnesota – it’s the heart of it all. Everything we do between now and November 3rd determines whether Democrats come together to defeat Donald Trump’s enablers, flip the House blue, and start holding this administration accountable, or whether we hand Republicans two more years of unchecked power. I’m fighting for that first version, and I’m leaving nothing to chance. There’s so much at stake. Just look at what this administration has done to our public health alone:They have undermined vaccines and contributed to the spread of preventable diseases like measles and whooping cough – and now hospitals nationwide are struggling to contain those outbreaks. They’ve gutted health research funding and brought the study of maternal health outcomes to a grinding halt. They are attacking our food safety infrastructure at the exact moment we need it most. They’ve tried to access Americans’ private medical records without consent to chase a debunked, non-existent link between vaccines and autism. They are reviewing the “safety” of mifepristone, a drug used safely by millions of women for decades. And they’ve harmed our ability to study and fight diseases abroad by withdrawing from the World Health Organization, gutting USAID, and ordering labs to stop studying diseases like Ebola in the middle of an outbreak. **I care deeply about public health – as a physician, as a mom, and as a human. I will never stop fighting for your right to access safe, science-backed health care, and I will never stop calling out the damage this administration is doing to the systems that keep us all safe.** That’s why I need your help right now. Our FEC filing deadline is on Wednesday, and I’m working hard to hit a big $20K online fundraising goal before then. Will you chip in so I can keep fighting for our public health in the halls of Congress? Kelly

clean_body: We are facing critical program gaps that could leave seats on the table and put a 2028 federal trifecta out of reach | | | | | Peter, if we fail to build back power at the state legislative level this fall, a Democratic federal trifecta in 2028 could be out of reach before the presidential race even begins. Democrats could win back Congress in 2026 and still lose the midterms. State legislatures elected this November will draw much of the 2028 House map. State legislatures will set the voting rules for 2028. State legislatures could introduce chaos into the certification of 2028 results. State legislatures could even make 2028 the first presidential election decided by the popular vote rather than the Electoral College. The DLCC has helped recruit a strong group of candidates to seize the opportunity to build power in our state legislatures this year, but we are facing critical program gaps that could leave seats on the table and put a 2028 federal trifecta out of reach. **** | If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process immediately. | | | | | | Thank you, Emily Emily Hogin Vice President and General Counsel Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee | Prepared and paid for by DLCC Victory Fund, 1301 K St NW, Suite 300W, Washington, DC 20005. Hey folks,
This one is about money, access, and the questions that come with being this close to power.
I dig into the reporting around Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding celebrations and Russian businessman Umar Kremlev, Trump's public response to the story, and the bigger questions I think this raises about conflicts of interest and accountability. We also get into how Republicans are responding--and why scrutiny of powerful political families matters no matter which party is in charge.
* [**00:01:15**] We dig into the reporting around Umar Kremlev, his background in Russia, and his relationship with Don Jr.
* [**00:04:46**] Trump responds to questions about his son's wedding and says Don Jr. paid Kremlev back--something I immediately challenge based on the reporting discussed in the episode.
* [**00:08:00**] CNN presses Sen. Bernie Moreno about the story, and his answer turns into a bigger conversation about how Republicans respond to allegations involving Trump's family.
* [**00:10:38**] We look at other examples involving Don Jr.'s business relationships and ask how private financial interests can intersect with public policy.
* [**00:11:49**] Sen. Adam Schiff challenges the Justice Department's response to the Kremlev story, bringing the episode back to the central question: who actually gets investigated when powerful people are involved?

This episode connects the wedding controversy to a much bigger issue: what happens when political power, family relationships, foreign money, and private business all collide. I'm staying focused on these stories because accountability matters, especially when the people involved have enormous influence over our government. I'm in a bit of a bind.
A recent poll shows that our race is now statistically tied, and the Senate GOP's top super PACs are pouring over $100 million into this race to defeat. That's because Senate control hinges on this battleground race.
Since I'm running a grassroots campaign, I can't fight back without you. **[So if you're able to chip in a few bucks to power our fight today before our critical end-of-quarter deadline, I'd really appreciate it. Here's the link to donate:](https://substack.com/redirect/68426408-8c25-47d2-bae7-b15a37f5db5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/68426408-8c25-47d2-bae7-b15a37f5db5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Now, my decision to run for Senate wasn't made lightly.
Serving as Governor was one of the great experiences of my life, but after my second term, I was ready to hang up my suit and tie. From adding hundreds of thousands of good-paying jobs to giving school teachers much-needed raises to expanding access to Medicaid, my #1 priority was to improve the lives of everyday people - and we did that.
That's why it's so upsetting to see how Washington DC insiders have turned their backs on hardworking people. Insiders like Michael Whatley, my opponent in this race.
My opponent says he'll lower costs, but he built his career promoting the interests of Big Oil and utility companies at the expense of working families. He says he'll protect our communities, but as chair of the state GOP, he appointed a convicted child sex offender who served six years in prison to powerful leadership roles within the party because he could raise money. He claims he'll fight for North Carolinians, but it's clear that his priority is choosing himself and his wealthy friends.
It's no wonder why the President anointed him to run after Thom Tillis bowed out of running for this seat.
So while I didn't plan to go to Washington DC, I couldn't stand by and watch the GOP rip away health care access, gut resources for public education and chip away at the middle class. They are not making this country "great again."
I had to get back in the fight, and I'm so glad I did.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/68426408-8c25-47d2-bae7-b15a37f5db5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Ever since launching this campaign, hundreds of thousands of folks like you have joined our grassroots movement for change, and momentum is on our side.
The hard part will be maintaining it for the next six weeks or so left in this race.
Republicans are spending over $100 million so far to turn voters against me and save their Senate majority - and this surge of dark money is taking a toll on our narrow polling lead.
We can fight back and win in North Carolina, but just as in elections past, I can't do it alone.
**[Please, will you chip in what you can today to help me flip this seat, retake the Senate for Democrats and return power in Washington DC to the hands of working families?](https://substack.com/redirect/68426408-8c25-47d2-bae7-b15a37f5db5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thanks for being on this team.
Roy Cooper

That's because Senate control hinges on this battleground race. Since I'm running a grassroots campaign, I can't fight back without you. Now, my decision to run for Senate wasn't made lightly. Serving as Governor was one of the great experiences of my life, but after my second term, I was ready to hang up my suit and tie. From adding hundreds of thousands of good-paying jobs to giving school teachers much-needed raises to expanding access to Medicaid, my #1 priority was to improve the lives of everyday people - and we did that. That's why it's so upsetting to see how Washington DC insiders have turned their backs on hardworking people. Insiders like Michael Whatley, my opponent in this race. My opponent says he'll lower costs, but he built his career promoting the interests of Big Oil and utility companies at the expense of working families. He says he'll protect our communities, but as chair of the state GOP, he appointed a convicted child sex offender who served six years in prison to powerful leadership roles within the party because he could raise money. He claims he'll fight for North Carolinians, but it's clear that his priority is choosing himself and his wealthy friends. It's no wonder why the President anointed him to run after Thom Tillis bowed out of running for this seat. So while I didn't plan to go to Washington DC, I couldn't stand by and watch the GOP rip away health care access, gut resources for public education and chip away at the middle class. They are not making this country "great again." I had to get back in the fight, and I'm so glad I did. Ever since launching this campaign, hundreds of thousands of folks like you have joined our grassroots movement for change, and momentum is on our side. The hard part will be maintaining it for the next six weeks or so left in this race. Republicans are spending over $100 million so far to turn voters against me and save their Senate majority - and this surge of dark money is taking a toll on our narrow polling lead. We can fight back and win in North Carolina, but just as in elections past, I can't do it alone. Thanks for being on this team. Roy Cooper | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Roy Cooper PO Box 1190, Raleigh, NC 27602 ? ?

Grassroots Update

SEPTEMBER 26, 2026

HI EVERYONE,

My name is Caleb, Director of Field and Campaign Operations with the MNGOP. I wanted to share a quick update on our field program
and, most importantly, let you know that you are already set up and can start helping today.

Recent polling shows two of our statewide candidates ahead, while the other three are neck and neck. In races this close, our
grassroots operation can make the difference. With enough volunteers making calls, knocking doors, and turning out Republican
voters, we have an opportunity to win statewide for the first time in 20 years.

You're Already Set Up on Right Insight

You're receiving this email because you've offered to volunteer with the MNGOP or one of our statewide campaigns. We've already
created a Right Insight account for you, so you don't need to wait for someone to get started.

Right Insight is the app we use for door knocking and phone calls. It gives you the voters to contact, the script to use, and
walks you through what to do based on each voter's response.

Getting started takes just a few minutes:

1. Download the Right Insight app.

2. Sign in using the email address where you received this message.

3. Right Insight will email you a six-digit verification code.

4. Enter the code and you're in. There is no password.

Once you're logged in, you'll see projects available to you.

Want to knock doors? Select Near Me to find voters near your current location.

Want to make calls? Select the call project for your Congressional District. Some Demuth volunteers may see projects for every
district. If so, choose your home district. If you aren't sure which district you're in, feel free to jump into CD 1 or CD 2.

For both calls and doors, simply open the questionnaire and the script is right there in the app. As you enter a voter's
responses, Right Insight will tell you what to ask next.

Never Called or Knocked Doors Before?

Right Insight is easy to learn, and we'll make sure you have opportunities to get comfortable with it. Our field directors will
host trainings, call banks, and door knocks around the state where you can learn alongside other volunteers.

Join Team Jude’s Adopt-A-Voter Postcard Project!**
Good morning,

We’re looking for volunteers to join Team Jude's **Adopt-A-Voter Postcard Project! **This is a simple and fun way to help Team Jude reach voters across Minnesota.

Volunteers will write short, personal notes reminding voters who have received—or will automatically receive—a ballot to **complete and return their ballot and vote for Tad Jude and the Republican team.
**
**Time matters!** The sooner we reach these voters, the sooner we can encourage them to complete and return their ballots. Sometimes, a friendly, personal reminder is all it takes to make sure a ballot doesn’t get set aside and forgotten.

The project is easy and can be done **individually, with friends and family, or as a group.** We’ve created a simple instruction sheet with everything you need, including step-by-step directions, suggested messages, and instructions for returning the completed postcards in the correct order.

And most importantly—**have fun with it!** Grab some friends, write some postcards, take some pictures, and help us reach voters throughout Minnesota.

Thank you for giving your time and energy to help Tad and our Republican team.

**We truly appreciate every volunteer and every postcard!
**
**Ready to help?**

Simply reply to this email, and a member of our Field Team will reach out to get you started!

Best,
**Team Jude**

**P.S.

Stay tuned!** Tad’s Field Team has **Voter Outreach Blitz Days** planned in communities across Minnesota. We hope you will help us get the vote out!

If you’re interested in helping reach voters by hosting a meet-and-greet, **making phone calls or door-knocking in your community** , email **[Volunteer@TadJude.com](mailto:Volunteer@TadJude.com)** or click the button below, and we’ll help you get started right away.

name: Swing Left
subject: Have you committed to The Big Swing Challenge yet?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
This GOTV season, we’re challenging you to take your biggest swing.
#
Hi there!
We want to make sure you didn’t miss the big announcement:
**This week, we launched The Big Swing Challenge to get as many people as possible involved in helping Democrats win big this year.**
There are millions of voters to talk with in swing districts and states across the country—the people who will decide the elections in these close races, and we’re going to need as much help as possible to reach them before Election Day.
That’s why we’re challenging every member of the Swing Left community to take your biggest swing this fall by getting out of your comfort zone and talking to as many voters as possible, whether you’ve volunteered before or this is your first time.
**Make sure to read below for more details,[and then click here to commit to the challenge today. We’ll follow up with more details soon!](http://act.swingleft.org/go/2385?utm_source=em20260926-2909&t=1&akid=2909%2E1562180%2EfvGF7f)**
Thank you,
The Swing Left Team
\-------- Forwarded message --------
From: Swing Left
Subject: Announcing The Big Swing Challenge!
Hi there,
Today marks 6 weeks until Election Day—the last day of voting in the midterm elections, which will have resounding consequences for 2028, 2030, and beyond.
Defeating MAGA at the ballot box this year is doable, but the final outcome will be up to us. If we win, and how big, will depend on each of us doing our part, including folks who have never canvassed or phone banked before—**which is why today, we’re announcing The Big Swing Challenge!**
**The Big Swing Challenge invites everyone to commit to taking action, set a personal goal, and then take your biggest swing by stepping out of your comfort zone and talking with as many voters as possible.**
[](http://act.swingleft.org/go/2385?utm_source=em20260926-2909&t=2&akid=2909%2E1562180%2EfvGF7f)
In this year’s midterm elections, we have a unique chance to shift the balance of power now AND for years to come. Our goal isn’t just to eke out a slim House majority; it’s to win the midterms decisively in the House, the Senate, and in key state races, by margins too large to contest, with majorities too strong to fracture and powerful enough for Democrats to actually govern.
**This is our chance to steer the direction of the county not just for the next two years, but for more than a decade to come.**
To make it happen, we need to persuade more people to vote for Democrats over Republicans, including people who’ve swung away from Dems in the past or are considering doing so now. That requires having more substantive conversations with voters and non-voters across the political spectrum—including Democrats, Republicans, and Independents—than ever before. And we’re going to get it done with Ground Truth.
Ground Truth is Swing Left’s innovative people-powered canvassing program where we focus on listening first. But these conversations and these big wins can only happen if you are on our team!
Chances are you live in or near one of our target swing districts or states. To take your big swing, you can join a canvass led by another volunteer, sign up to host your own, or, with the training we’ll give you, go canvass in your nearest swing district whenever works best for you.
Millions of voters in swing districts and states across the country have never had a Democratic campaign knock on their door because of limited resources and too-narrow targeting. If we each call, knock on doors, or talk to a few voters (or a lot!), we can collectively drive wins in close races and make sustained political change possible.
The Big Swing Challenge is an opportunity for all of us to take action and see what we can accomplish when thousands of people across the country take their biggest swing together.
[**If you’re ready to take part, click here to commit to the challenge today. We’ll share weekly updates on what you and other Big Swing Challenge takers are accomplishing, volunteer leaderboards, tips on talking with voters, and opportunities to volunteer in a swing district or state near you!**](http://act.swingleft.org/go/2385?utm_source=em20260926-2909&t=3&akid=2909%2E1562180%2EfvGF7f)
**[Commit To The Big Swing Challenge](http://act.swingleft.org/go/2385?utm_source=em20260926-2909&t=4&akid=2909%2E1562180%2EfvGF7f)**
The Swing Left community comprises thousands of committed volunteers and grassroots donors nationwide. There’s power in our numbers. Six weeks from now, we’ll know what we accomplished together. So let’s show up, talk with as many voters as possible by phone, door-to-door, and online, and turn out voters in swing districts across the country.
We have the power to organize, persuade, and shape the balance of power for years to come.
Thank you for taking the challenge with us—let’s get out there and win back the House, the Senate, and key state races this year to restore the national balance of power!
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20260926-2&t=5&refcode2=2909_1562180_fvGF7f&akid=2909%2E1562180%2EfvGF7f)

body:
Charlie saw something rare in JD Vance | | | |
---
| | | Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

clean_body: Charlie saw something rare in JD Vance | | | | | | | Patriot, Faith is essential to the survival and success of America. Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth. He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him. He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith. Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story... It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now. So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together. Young people face that pressure every single day. They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is. JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion. He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back. That's what Communion is about... And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now. #
Peter,
**Arizona, Georgia, and Texas have their voter registration deadlines coming up on October 5th.**
Registering eligible Latino voters in these battleground states requires a huge amount of resources. **That’s why we set a goal of raising $250,000 before October 5th to make sure our teams on the ground can reach as many people as possible.**
Because of this community, we’re already 52% of the way to our goal. When you make a donation to emails like this one, your donation goes straight toward powering our voter registration drives from now through October 5th.

clean_body: | | | | | Peter , I flew above battlefields, passing burning husks of armored vehicles, and in Iraq I poured enough sand out of my boots to fill a desert. You would think that after flying an Apache helicopter through an active war zone, and having God knows how many stray bullets shot my direction, there’s not a thing on this planet that could scare me. I thought so too, until my team reminded me about what’s coming in the next few days. Let me explain. This campaign’s bigger than anything I’ve done in Iraq. Rather than covering for a team on the ground, the fate of more than 10 million people will be decided in November. Campaigning isn’t easy, and sometimes it feels like the weight of the world is on my shoulders. Just before I typed this email, my team reminded me about our upcoming End-of-Month fundraising deadline. This isn’t just an arbitrary deadline; this is one of our last BIG goals before the November election. I’m not going to ask you to dig deep into your pockets. All I’m asking is a $1 or more donation, which will go right into my campaign's war chest and help me and President Trump take down the Democrat machine come November. As a combat veteran and a patriot - I give you my word that every dollar matters, and I’m eternally thankful for ANY gift you can make. Time is running out. | | Today is Public Lands Day. But what should be a day to celebrate our treasured outdoor spaces and national parks is a reminder of something much more sinister: Trump's endless attacks on our public lands and attempts to give them away for the benefit of corporations. **During his second term, Trump has moved to strip more than 86 million acres of public land of their federal protections. His priorities? Resource extraction, privatization, and commercial development for new data centers.** Last June, we were able to stave off attempts to force the sale of nearly 3 million acres of public land, but our work is not done. The Trump administration is currently reviewing proposals that would open up over 17,000 acres of public lands across Arizona, Idaho, Nevada, Utah, Wyoming, and Oregon for development of data centers. Public lands belong to you, the taxpayers. Not Trump and not corporations. Not only do we have a right to know what is being discussed, but many communities have made their opinions clear: _Keep Your Hands Off Our Public Lands_. Our public lands are essential to our identity as Oregonians. But this administration thinks it can silently and secretly auction them off for the benefit of billionaires, so corporations can turn these spaces into new data centers and mining operations. **Our Public Lands are not their personal gold mine.** On Public Lands Day and every day, I remain committed to protecting our natural treasures. clean_body: | | | | Today is Public Lands Day. But what should be a day to celebrate our treasured outdoor spaces and national parks is a reminder of something much more sinister: Trump's endless attacks on our public lands and attempts to give them away for the benefit of corporations. During his second term, Trump has moved to strip more than 86 million acres of public land of their federal protections. His priorities? Resource extraction, privatization, and commercial development for new data centers. Last June, we were able to stave off attempts to force the sale of nearly 3 million acres of public land, but our work is not done. The Trump administration is currently reviewing proposals that would open up over 17,000 acres of public lands across Arizona, Idaho, Nevada, Utah, Wyoming, and Oregon for development of data centers. Public lands belong to you, the taxpayers. Not Trump and not corporations. Not only do we have a right to know what is being discussed, but many communities have made their opinions clear: Keep Your Hands Off Our Public Lands. Our public lands are essential to our identity as Oregonians. But this administration thinks it can silently and secretly auction them off for the benefit of billionaires, so corporations can turn these spaces into new data centers and mining operations. Our Public Lands are not their personal gold mine. On Public Lands Day and every day, I remain committed to protecting our natural treasures. body:
Is this the year Florida turns blue?
Friend,
The New York Times ran a piece asking a question that would have sounded impossible two years ago: **is this the year Florida turns blue?**
They watched us flip the Miami mayor's office, a long-shot State Senate seat, and even the State House district that covers Mar-a-Lago. And they came away taking David's campaign seriously, because they see what we see: **Florida is ready for a new direction.**
**[When the national press starts paying attention, so do our opponents. So we have to ask: will you chip in $5 between our campaign and Aaron Ford right now to keep this momentum going?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260926_1_ak.gHRDEF&amount=5&refcode=em20260926-952&t=2&akid=952%2E127862%2ECAdlgs)**
Here's what David has been saying on the road. _We’re winning._
We know how that sounds in a state that hasn't elected a Democratic Governor in a generation. But David has been in every corner of Florida, and what he's hearing is that people are exhausted. They're tired of the culture wars, the toxicity, and leaders who pick fights instead of solving problems.
What they want is someone laser-focused on the cost of housing, health care, and electricity. They want someone who focus on the things that unite us, and on tackling the issues we all face together.
Here's the catch, and the Times printed this too. Our opponent Byron Donalds has raised a massive warchest, and he's hoping to spend his way to victory.
The GOP is ready to pour hundreds of millions of dollars into this race, bankrolled by the special interests that have run Tallahassee for thirty years. They'll spend whatever it takes to ensure they hold on to power.
We are not going to match them dollar for dollar. We don't have to.
**What we have to do is the work, neighbor to neighbor, conversation by conversation, all across this state. That's how we built this moment, and that's how we protect it.**
**[So we're asking: can you split a donation today to keep this moving?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260926_1_ak.gHRDEF&amount=5&refcode=em20260926-952&t=3&akid=952%2E127862%2ECAdlgs)**

Thank you for your support, today and every day.
Team David Jolly

The Regime Open — September 25, 2026
Iran Named a Deadline. The US and China Just Moved Theirs.
Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within seven days of a deal; Washington wants nuclear talks first. Trump and Xi bought two more months on trade. Neither story resolved — and yields hit a fresh 19-year high regardless.
|
---
Thursday delivered concrete outcomes on both of the diplomatic tracks this newsletter has followed all week — and both landed as extensions of the status quo rather than breakthroughs. **Verified fact:** Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi announced a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days of U.S. acceptance, saying “the Strait of Hormuz would be open on the end of the seventh day and [peace] talks would restart,” a proposal resembling the collapsed June memorandum. Secretary of State Rubio cautioned against calling the talks “a major breakthrough.” Separately, Trump and Xi extended their tariff truce through January 10, leaving Taiwan, AI, and rare-earth questions unresolved. Equities were roughly flat — S&P; 500 -0.07%, Nasdaq -0.06%, Dow -0.32% — while oil rose (WTI +1.04% to $93.12, Brent +1.53% to $104.70) and the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.192%, its highest since 2007.
| | Regime Signal 01 — Iran's Offer Is Concrete, But the Disagreement Is Structural, Not Cosmetic
---|---
**Verified fact:** Washington wants Iran's nuclear program addressed immediately; Iran insists on sequencing — reopening the strait first, nuclear talks later. **Our interpretation:** this is a genuine, specific proposal with a genuine, specific sticking point, which is a meaningful upgrade in precision over weeks of vaguer diplomatic signaling. But a sequencing disagreement this fundamental — what comes first, sanctions relief or nuclear verification — has derailed comparable frameworks before, including the June memorandum this plan explicitly echoes.
| | Regime Signal 02 — A Trade Truce Extension Is a Deadline Deferral, Not a Resolution
---|---
**Verified fact:** the new January 10 deadline replaces the November 10 rare-earth deadline this newsletter flagged as the key date to watch, buying roughly two additional months without resolving the underlying disagreements on Taiwan, AI, or rare-earth export policy. **Our interpretation:** extending a deadline under pressure, as both sides did here, is meaningfully different from resolving what the deadline was about — it removes near-term uncertainty while leaving the substantive dispute fully intact for a later date.
| | Regime Signal 03 — The Bond Market Isn't Waiting for Either Story to Resolve
---|---
**Verified fact:** the 10-year yield's move to 5.192% and the 30-year's move to 5.476% — its highest since 2004 — came on the same day as both diplomatic developments, with oil rising rather than falling. **Our interpretation:** this is now the third consecutive session of broad-based yield strength this newsletter has tracked, increasingly independent of whether the week's diplomatic news is positive or negative — the clearest evidence yet that a structural rate repricing, not day-to-day headlines, is now the dominant driver.
| | This Week’s Confirmation Point
---|---
Whether Washington formally responds to Iran's seven-day Hormuz proposal, and whether the sequencing disagreement (strait first vs. nuclear first) narrows or hardens in the coming days.

| | Dear Friend who has common sense,I'm always going to stand with America.I'm always going to reject the extremes. I'm always going to reject Socialism.I'm always going to fight against the anti-American way of life.And this has enraged a lot of people in the media, in my party, and even former staffers --- disgruntled leakers who are viciously and anonymously attacking me. This is what happens when you put common sense and the wellbeing of the people you are supposed to represent ahead of party loyalty.But most of all, I think this is what happens when you clash with the Socialist movement "DSA!" that is hijacking the Democratic party. They want to...Abolish our bordersAbolish the electoral collegeAbolish IsraelAbolish the Senate and the Supreme Court (no, seriously, this is in the "DSA!" platform)That bad news is the "DSA!" crazies have gone from the political fringe to controlling one of America's major political parties—and onto ballots across the country.The good news is the hardworking, common-sense Americans I talk to every day still aren't buying it.I mean, a recent Rasmussen poll kind of proves it:71% of Americans reject socialism67% of Democrat voters reject socialism While 82% of Republican voters reject socialismBut here's the thing. The loudest voice in the room is often the one that looks the most powerful.And I've got to say, the "DSA!" voices in Washington are loud and getting louder. The media is their megaphone. Which is why you may be under the false impression that people really do want the "DSA!" and their extreme policiesNothing could be further from the truth.**[I'm standing up to them.](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckcFunDAQhp_G3LwyY2dYDhyoWKJW3RalUnq0BnuWuAKMjDdR376iTV6g10__P5pP_8-rvVKYwzp9o4WbKW6bTbsNC81v9HufYlinHBP_Ypf36IIFBShVLQEtuRxe2RoqfGMIDSIW3JRVrYyuUWHx0nhU6D1XJRg1GlOr2vkbmrIq0UF9VkVojoOqBiwRlDKnEh5GUGB0zXjzMAqj2Icc0-n4LfEePK850HxycSnm5iXnbRe6FdAL6Hd298QnWtnHfCQE9DfOmdNCq7zFJDcS0G9U-ZIfCNnL8uxGaUo6y3HUJJ3XHpTnyp1R6P6eF7vHe3IsdPd0eRaAB1rYh_sidHe5tp-_vkNHy0ZhWoXu3qXAfuoe7Zd-aO3T5dn-Dduh_THIoZWP34fhoxnXzGsWujug_GgXqfHbW5jnsGMljJoWCv-88_8u9drAnwAAAP__g8-epQ)** But sadly I'm pretty much alone on this side of the aisle.So, can I ask you a favor? Whatever your party affiliation is, can I ask you to stand with me against the daily barrage of hit-pieces **[If you can donate just $25 it would be a big help to me.](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckcFunDAQhp_G3LwyY2dYDhyoWKJW3RalUnq0BnuWuAKMjDdR376iTV6g10__P5pP_8-rvVKYwzp9o4WbKW6bTbsNC81v9HufYlinHBP_Ypf36IIFBShVLQEtuRxe2RoqfGMIDSIW3JRVrYyuUWHx0nhU6D1XJRg1GlOr2vkbmrIq0UF9VkVojoOqBiwRlDKnEh5GUGB0zXjzMAqj2Icc0-n4LfEePK850HxycSnm5iXnbRe6FdAL6Hd298QnWtnHfCQE9DfOmdNCq7zFJDcS0G9U-ZIfCNnL8uxGaUo6y3HUJJ3XHpTnyp1R6P6eF7vHe3IsdPd0eRaAB1rYh_sidHe5tp-_vkNHy0ZhWoXu3qXAfuoe7Zd-aO3T5dn-Dduh_THIoZWP34fhoxnXzGsWujug_GgXqfHbW5jnsGMljJoWCv-88_8u9drAnwAAAP__g8-epQ)** But it will also send a message. It will show the truth that the "real numbers" are on our side here in Pennsylvania, as well as around the rest of America. You know, I recently stood in front of the iconic U.S. Steel Mill and recorded a video talking about how my friend Dave McCormick and I banded together with President Trump to save this facility and the larger steel industry. But I'm not backing down.Even though I know the media... the "DSA!"... and the party bosses... are going to try even harder to defeat me:
---
**"Fetterman Draws Shadow Primary From Democrats Eager to Replace Him: The Pennsylvania senator has long irked members of his own party" ~ Bloomberg**
---
If you'll stand with me today, I know we can show them that we're not backing down and that the real numbers are on the side of common sense and putting our country first.Thank you!John Fetterman P.S. - I'll bet you're more than a little surprised to get this email from me. So, I want to say thanks for setting aside party affiliation for a second and hearing me out. You see, I'm not a progressive. And I'm definitely not a Democratic Socialist. I'm just a senator with a big mouth who happens to stand for common-sense things like... strong borders, safe streets, a powerful economy, bringing jobs to my constituents, and Israel and Ukraine's right to defend themselves, not to mention the basic machinery of our democracy (the Electoral College, the Senate, and the Supreme Court). If you see eye-to-eye with me, then I could sure use your help. The "DSA!" vision for Pennsylvania and for America is not a healthy one. It is a dangerous one.Common-sense people need to join together now to reject this vision before it's too late. **[Can I count on you to stand with me today?](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckcFunDAQhp_G3LwyY2dYDhyoWKJW3RalUnq0BnuWuAKMjDdR376iTV6g10__P5pP_8-rvVKYwzp9o4WbKW6bTbsNC81v9HufYlinHBP_Ypf36IIFBShVLQEtuRxe2RoqfGMIDSIW3JRVrYyuUWHx0nhU6D1XJRg1GlOr2vkbmrIq0UF9VkVojoOqBiwRlDKnEh5GUGB0zXjzMAqj2Icc0-n4LfEePK850HxycSnm5iXnbRe6FdAL6Hd298QnWtnHfCQE9DfOmdNCq7zFJDcS0G9U-ZIfCNnL8uxGaUo6y3HUJJ3XHpTnyp1R6P6eF7vHe3IsdPd0eRaAB1rYh_sidHe5tp-_vkNHy0ZhWoXu3qXAfuoe7Zd-aO3T5dn-Dduh_THIoZWP34fhoxnXzGsWujug_GgXqfHbW5jnsGMljJoWCv-88_8u9drAnwAAAP__g8-epQ)**

Policy Transmission — September 25, 2026
The Trump-Xi Summit Did Exactly What Low Expectations Predicted
A two-month trade truce extension, a warm handshake, and Taiwan, AI, and rare earths all still unresolved — the summit matched its muted preview almost point for point.
|
---
| | The Mechanism
---|---
This newsletter flagged Thursday's Trump-Xi summit as arriving with already-discounted expectations. The actual outcome matched that muted baseline almost exactly: enough progress to avoid a breakdown, not enough to resolve anything substantive.
| | What Was Actually Agreed
---|---
**Verified fact:** Trump and Xi's trade officials extended their tariff truce through January 10, replacing the November 10 rare-earth export deadline this newsletter has tracked for a week. Xi received what was described as “a rare planeside greeting” from Trump, a symbolic gesture of goodwill. **Reported claim:** Taiwan's pending $14 billion arms package, AI cooperation, and the underlying rare-earth export dispute all remain unresolved per multiple summit recaps.
| | Regime Classification: PRESSURE, Deferred Rather Than Resolved
---|---
**Our interpretation:** a two-month extension is a rational outcome for two sides that, as one Bloomberg headline put it, are “neither able to afford a fight” — it buys time without requiring either side to concede on Taiwan or rare earths. **What remains unknown** is whether the additional two months produces genuine progress on the harder issues, or simply moves the same unresolved cliff edge from November to January, when markets will face the identical uncertainty with less runway to negotiate a further extension.
| | Why the Symbolic Gesture Matters Less Than the Deadline
---|---
A warm greeting photographs well but does not bind either government to a substantive position. **Next confirmation point:** any concrete movement on the Taiwan arms package or rare-earth licensing specifics in the weeks following the summit, which would distinguish genuine progress from a simple deadline extension.

Families who already qualify through one program should not have to fight through red tape to get help feeding their kids.
**The WIC for Kids Act will:**
* **Grant automatic WIC eligibility** to families already participating in programs like SNAP, Medicaid, CHIP, and Head Start.
* Help align certification periods **so families can consolidate appointments and stay enrolled.**
* **Direct states to include plans** for serving kinship families.

This bill is endorsed by the National WIC Association, the Food Research and Action Center, Connecticut Foodshare, and other advocates working to end hunger.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: We're in the lead, Peter.
body:
First, we brought this race to a tie. Now, we have taken the lead.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, this poll actually made me do a double take:
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260926_2_maristpoll.m6VjLp&refcode=em20260926-2241&amount=5&t=1&akid=2241%2E299639%2Eih4rGn)
ANOTHER poll was released this week showing me _leading_ this race for Texas governor. **NPR/Marist has me at 49%, with Abbott behind at 46%.**
This is not a fluke, Peter. It’s the *second* poll in less than a week showing that we have pulled ahead of Greg Abbott. **[Please rush a $5 donation so we can flip Texas blue.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260926_2_maristpoll.m6VjLp&refcode=em20260926-2241&amount=5&t=2&akid=2241%2E299639%2Eih4rGn)**
The electoral landscape in Texas is shifting beneath our feet. A few months ago, every poll had us down. But as we’ve successfully reached persuadable voters across all 254 Texas counties, we have done something remarkable:
First, we brought this race to a tie. **Now, we have taken the lead.**
Meanwhile, Abbott’s numbers are going in the exact opposite direction. His approval rating is underwater. His favorability is underwater. _Never_ in Abbott’s twelve year career as governor has he been more vulnerable than he is today, and his top campaign advisors have admitted outright they believe our race will be close on Election Day.
But this week, Abbott unleashed a $12 MILLION wave of attack ads against me — his first negative ad spending of the entire campaign. The more scared of losing Republicans become, the more money they will throw at us to mislead voters and erase our real chance at victory. And the truth is: they have enough money to swing this race back in their favor.
**That’s why we set an emergency goal of raising $2,000,000 by Wednesday. And this goal is not negotiable. That’s the _minimum_ amount we need to respond to Abbott’s flood of negative TV and radio ads. **
Abbott’s attack ads are being aired across Texas as you read this email. So we have no time to waste if we want to hold onto our lead and win.
**[Please help me close our fundraising gap by chipping in $5 right now so we can reach our $2,000,000 goal and defeat Greg Abbott on November 3rd.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260926_2_maristpoll.m6VjLp&refcode=em20260926-2241&amount=5&t=3&akid=2241%2E299639%2Eih4rGn)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260926_2_maristpoll.m6VjLp&amount=5&refcode=em20260926-2241&t=22&akid=2241%2E299639%2Eih4rGn)
Thank you,
Gina

Their attack ads will go live any day now, and the only way we’ll have the resources to respond is by reaching our $5 million end-of-quarter goal ASAP. We don’t want to sound like the sky is falling or sound the alarm unnecessarily – but unfortunately, this is not one of those times. Our grassroots campaign is being outspent. | Letter from the Chair
---
| Friends,
From the day I became NEGOP Chairman, one mission has guided everything we do: unite this party for a fight we all knew was coming. Midterms are hard on the party holding Washington. History is not on our side unless we make it so.
We are as united as I have ever seen us -- not around personalities, but around a shared duty: defend Nebraska from the sharp left turn Democrats have taken these last two years.
We still have the Good Life. Not a perfect life. A good one.
Safe communities. Neighbors who show up. Extraordinary common sense. No boys in girls' sports. Meritocracy instead of DEI. Secure borders versus open borders. That is worth protecting and defending. It is also easy to take for granted. When life is good, complacency creeps in. Apathy looks like "someone else will handle it."
This year, that excuse is gone. Across the ballot, Democrat candidates have shown that what they say in Nebraska is not what they mean once the cameras are off. People who were sleepwalking through this election have woken up. Momentum is with us. Momentum dies if we ease off.
None of our work matters if you do not vote -- and if you do not bring your friends and family with you.
The NEGOP, our county parties, and Republican campaigns are already on the doors, on the phones, writing postcards, and sending texts. There is a job for every temperament and every schedule. You can call or text from anywhere in the state. For the first time, NE.GOP has a statewide candidate slate (see below) that you can sort by county. Find your races. Share them. Use them.
We are not doing this alone. Republicans and right-leaning groups are pulling the same direction: keep the radical left from gaining ground in Nebraska. TPUSA Action has been mailing voter-registration pieces -- I received one myself. Citizens for Free Enterprise is knocking doors here and in other states. PACs are funding campaigns and putting voter information in people's hands. Faith communities are awake and moving their members.
Thirty-nine days. November 3 is not far off. Make every one of those days count. Donate to a campaign. Vote. Take someone with you. Knock a door. Make a call. Send a text. Defend the Good Life.
Together we win!
In Liberty and in Truth,
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

| A Message From Senator Pete Ricketts...
I'm Proud to Fight for Rural Nebraska. Dan Osborn Mocks Rural Nebraska. Over the last month I've had the chance to travel across Nebraska and hear from the people I serve. Hardworking Nebraskans told me what matters most to them.
Every stop showed exactly why Nebraska is worth fighting to protect. In North Platte, Sustainable Beef processes 1,500 cattle a day. It contributes $1 billion to the local economy. We fought to make that producer-owned facility a reality. In Kearney, a new health education complex is training more doctors and nurses. We secured $60 million for that project. We have also brought jobs to Columbus, Blair, and communities across the state. It was great to see these investments paying off.
Back in Washington, we are delivering. I helped pass the historic tax cuts keeping more money in your pocket. I have fought to secure the border and enforce our immigration laws. I have stood up for Nebraska farmers and ranchers. We are expanding markets and increasing demand for homegrown biofuels.
The choice this November is clear. I love rural Nebraska. I have spent my career delivering for it. Dan Osborn sees it differently. The [Omaha World-Herald reported on audio](https://feyrpzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001iNDDt4xpbNsED-xVL7gy0Xk7sBPgHmUVDhqxbWiiWzRNYnzuyJNFVSVam8ImTHgzwD0j5oNpOz0wLuH4-VqXHzM6ClvXfPKqcsOLKKW0pmFhsXsUZMbyzbIiolccrmEcf2GkqZRmQIssoGqj1U1ZGmOU0BJeDS9nTSGGjzRiphkKyKa99I7GpIP2-JkljHZiJn8p58kUMxLuY-Rta7c4LY4uDHlfudd2nsZFJo-42CyXYsg-6BUOdnkfSbzEh6mMgq2Xgm0OvGAEPCUSe-JjKhPMDa-KxDp7zFUuon7errMoDZ0dx5HmkE1615cwAeixB8kWdVxHeoU=&c=rtrGAdTYA4Wl-ZPf0RO1_YLBvCrKjYEwzDOA5fls-I_b0PAIyOe1qw==&ch=ktSWIS4My8QOWw1PM5yw5SHeoA8zRV_iDEtrytGr5_mon6RRRTRZgA==) of Dan Osborn describing rural Nebraskans. He thinks their lives "probably suck so f---ing bad." That is what he thinks of rural voters when he believes the microphone is off.
The people of rural Nebraska are the backbone of this state. I am proud to serve them. Osborn mocks them. I fight for them. That is the choice in November.
Stay united. Get out and vote. Bring everyone you know with you. Visit [PeteRicketts.com](https://feyrpzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001iNDDt4xpbNsED-xVL7gy0Xk7sBPgHmUVDhqxbWiiWzRNYnzuyJNFVSVam8ImTHgzvjhZF54MsvXOx-iQpRu9UuE8IQ3fhfJarebjNJR8iH8CJl1GnVS5muNOFUykhUxphiwiBaIab-PAqZZAoqviGg==&c=rtrGAdTYA4Wl-ZPf0RO1_YLBvCrKjYEwzDOA5fls-I_b0PAIyOe1qw==&ch=ktSWIS4My8QOWw1PM5yw5SHeoA8zRV_iDEtrytGr5_mon6RRRTRZgA==) to volunteer and get involved this November.
Senator Pete Ricketts

We'll hand Democrats their first statewide win in Texas since 1994, and the earthquake will be felt by Americans across the country. First, let's be clear about how we got here. The Republican establishment in DC spent over $150 million — the most expensive Senate primary in American history — trying to stop Ken Paxton from becoming the nominee. _They lost._ Paxton defeated Sen. John Cornyn by nearly 30 points. But the damage was done, and now Democrat James Talarico is within striking distance of flipping the seat. You'd think Cornyn would be all-in to stop him from turning Texas blue. Nope. Instead, he's trashing Paxton as lazy and a poor campaigner, while telling reporters the party shouldn't spend another dime on his race because of limited resources. That's rich. **Even worse, Cornyn is working with former President George W. Bush to pull money out of Texas to fund moderate Senate candidates in other states — many of whom are far bigger underdogs than Paxton.** With friends like these, who needs enemies?

He sued the Biden administration more than any other AG in the country — on the border, on illegal mandates, on federal overreach — and won. While career politicians in Washington cut deals, Paxton has been on the front lines of the fight against the open-borders agenda. President Trump didn't endorse him as an afterthought — he called Paxton a "true MAGA warrior" because Paxton has earned it. That's exactly why the establishment tried to kill his campaign before it started and why they're throwing a temper tantrum now. A real fighter in the Senate threatens the comfortable do-nothing environment they've built in DC. They'd rather have an empty suit who plays along with their empty promises and endless excuses than a conservative who delivers. **Make no mistake: John Cornyn and the GOP establishment are working against Paxton because they want Texas to lose. clean_body: The RINOs in Texas are still throwing a fit over losing to Ken Paxton. | | | | | Fellow Conservative: Texas is about to decide the fate of the Senate majority — and if we lose it, we won't just lose a seat. We'll hand Democrats their first statewide win in Texas since 1994, and the earthquake will be felt by Americans across the country. First, let's be clear about how we got here. The Republican establishment in DC spent over $150 million — the most expensive Senate primary in American history — trying to stop Ken Paxton from becoming the nominee. They lost. Paxton defeated Sen. John Cornyn by nearly 30 points. But the damage was done, and now Democrat James Talarico is within striking distance of flipping the seat. You'd think Cornyn would be all-in to stop him from turning Texas blue. Nope. Instead, he's trashing Paxton as lazy and a poor campaigner, while telling reporters the party shouldn't spend another dime on his race because of limited resources. That's rich. Even worse, Cornyn is working with former President George W. Bush to pull money out of Texas to fund moderate Senate candidates in other states — many of whom are far bigger underdogs than Paxton. With friends like these, who needs enemies? Ken Paxton has spent over a decade as Texas Attorney General doing what the GOP establishment only talks about. He sued the Biden administration more than any other AG in the country — on the border, on illegal mandates, on federal overreach — and won. While career politicians in Washington cut deals, Paxton has been on the front lines of the fight against the open-borders agenda. President Trump didn't endorse him as an afterthought — he called Paxton a "true MAGA warrior" because Paxton has earned it. That's exactly why the establishment tried to kill his campaign before it started and why they're throwing a temper tantrum now. A real fighter in the Senate threatens the comfortable do-nothing environment they've built in DC. They'd rather have an empty suit who plays along with their empty promises and endless excuses than a conservative who delivers. Make no mistake: John Cornyn and the GOP establishment are working against Paxton because they want Texas to lose. They need it to lose, so they can point at the wreckage and say, "See? Only RINOs can win." It's a self-fulfilling prophecy. They know the game. Give conservative voters a choice between a Democrat and a RINO, and we'll hold our nose and vote RINO. But give us a choice between a Democrat and a real conservative, and the establishment would rather watch us lose than let us win on our own terms. It was never about winning a majority; it was about maintaining their control over the party. Senate Conservatives Fund exists for exactly this fight — to back conservative candidates in the races the party committees have already written off, when the committees would rather protect their own than protect the country. You can donate to SCF to support our independent efforts to elect Ken Paxton, and you can contribute directly to his campaign. It's the best way to help conservatives win in Texas. Friend, we know we’ve been reaching out a lot, but there’s a reason we’re asking again today. We’re at a point in this race where we are making tough decisions that have a real impact on what we’re able to do in the weeks ahead. _Let us explain:_
**1.** The latest poll shows Deb’s race is**closer than anyone expected.
****
2.** Republicans see this race as a **top pickup opportunity,** especially knowing New Mexico’s governorship tends to flip parties every eight years.

**3.** Deb’s Republican opponent is bankrolled by many of Trump’s TOP supporters in New Mexico and is focused on bringing Trump’s extremism to New Mexico.
Between now and Election Day, keeping our ads on TV, traveling across New Mexico, organizing events, and reaching voters takes real resources. **And the closer we get to Election Day, the more quickly those decisions and investments have to be made.** _None of us want to look back the morning after Election Day wishing we’d done a little more. Because the stakes couldn’t be higher — for our working families, our public lands, and our kids’ and grandkids’ futures._
That’s why you’re hearing from us again — because what happens right now will shape what we’re able to do in the final stretch. [**Friend, will you chip in $5 — or whatever you can spare — right now to elect Deb this November and deliver progress for New Mexico’s working families?**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16410?refcode=jtk1445-fr-nd&t=2&akid=12702%2E400544%2EVWCGR-)

On Friday, my family and I went to the local mosque to hear three people speak. Jamil, Mae, and Avner - **two Palestinians, and a former Israeli soldier.**
They were there as "Combatants for Peace," and I recommend [their work](https://substack.com/redirect/ac2af76e-047d-4c4a-a34b-3603a2fdd720?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
As a lifelong advocate for peace and justice for the Palestinian people, I'll admit I entered with some skepticism. _**After everything the IDF has done, how could this collaboration be sincere? How could this be trusted?**_
Let's just say, I left with more grounded hope for peace that I've felt in a long time.
Let me tell you what they had to say.
_Note, please, that this essay is my direct personal recollection of their presentation, shared as such -- not intended to be an ultimate, perfect, or formally approved distillation of their life stories. I fully expect that some details are incorrect; but I have reproduced the content and spirit of their messages to the best of my ability._

Mae spoke first. She is a Palestinian woman, perhaps sixty, with wide and gentle eyes, short grey hair, and a clear gaze. She started by telling us how she grew up in Bethlehem - in the occupied West Bank - before the occupation was severe.
When she was small, she could walk fifteen minutes to the Dome of the Rock - or run twenty minutes to Al Aqsa. Jerusalem was open to everyone, and she spoke with deep feeling about how sacred that was -- everyone, of all faiths, shared in the holidays, met international travelers who came to Jerusalem from all over the world. Palestinian, Israeli, Muslim, Christian, Jew, the city was open to all. Only later on, did the restrictions come into place.
One of her parents had a blue card, the other a green card. That means, in the pseudo apartheid system of Israeli civil society, that as the restrictions grew worse, eventually her mother and father could not live together. (Later, she and her husband, also, could not live in the same location, and she still faces restrictions in daily life on whether she can see her daughter, because of this.)
When the restrictions came down, now suddenly she couldn't take a sunny afternoon run to the third-holiest place in Islam. She couldn't go to visit her family, who lived fifteen minutes' walk away, in the Old City. The restriction, division, and military oppression landed on her and her family directly.
Naturally, she resisted. She was angry, and hurting, and who wouldn't be? She threw rocks. She became active in the resistance. Fighting consumed her, for quite some time, until one day her mother asked her, "**Habibi (dear one), who are you going to kill to free Jerusalem?** "
She said, "Mama, it is not in my heart to kill anyone, I'm just trying to fight for freedom peace." Her mother admonished her, and said "Darling, when your goals do not match your actions, it does not matter what your goals are. **Your actions are what you are creating, and right now, you are creating violence.** If you truly want to build peace, then go get an education, become a therapist, learn about trauma, and come back and be a counselor to us, to the Palestinians. Help our people with this pain; help build a better way."
So she did. She found a way to leave Palestine, and studied trauma, and came back a practicing counselor. She married a man who had an Israeli card, whereas she had a Palestinian one, which prevented them from living together under the Israeli system of occupation. It was in seeking a way to live with her husband that she first learned about shared communities, where Palestinians and Israelis have found ways to live together. She told us that her first visit to one of those communities, was her first time _ever_ encountering and speaking with a normal Jewish Israeli person, who was not in uniform and not actively exerting military force over her and her people.
From those early conversations, which helped her see the shared humanity of both communities, she began to understand that they are "cousins." Truly, she said. She told us that no one knows the Israelis better than the Palestinians - their home life, their food, their culture, their ways of thinking - and, that the Israelis know her better than any other people on earth. She began to see that **togetherness was the antidote,** and that the real enemy was not each other, but the _system_ that told them they must hate and fear each other.
Later in the afternoon, she spoke about how that **togetherness is the strongest defensive and creative power they possess.** When she travels internationally with her Jewish Israeli brothers and sisters in Combatants for Peace, what is anyone going to say at any border? What charge of antisemitism could ever be made to stick?
She's not fighting anyone. She doesn't hate anyone. They're together, now, working and organizing and protesting and sharing their stories and striving, together, against the system that imposes war, violence, and separation -- striving for peace.

Then, Avner spoke. Avner is 50 years old - he was born in 1976, in an Israeli kibbutz. He described a collective, socialist, agricultural upbringing, with apparent fondness. His father was a pacifist in his civilian life - and, specifically, opposed the occupation.
> _**An Israeli father in a Kibbutz, opposing the occupation of Palestine.**_
As Avner described it, his father, and he, initially blamed the occupation on "the settlers," not identifying any role in it themselves. But... as an adult Israeli man, his father was also a reservist in the IDF. They all were. **One month per year, his father was a soldier in uniform, obeying orders, carrying out military missions in service to the state of Israel.**
This contradiction was accepted with a shrug. Of course you were going to serve in the Army, everyone did, everyone had to, and you carried out the mission you were assigned -- _**what else were you going to do?**_
Avner and his friends grew up knowing, without question, that at the age of 18 they would go off to the Army. And they did. Avner was honest about describing his enthusiasm at that age, and his idiocy, and his ignorance -- he became part of a well-known commando unit, and yes it was about patriotism and service and all of that, but it was also good with the girls.
He told us that his unit was not assigned to carry out the dirty work of occupation, so **even after his mandatory two years, he did not really know the extent of the military occupation that Palestinians were living under.** He had been told, relentlessly, from a young age, that he and his family were in danger, and their military was protecting them. He had **never** , in his life, met or spoken with a Palestinian.
Until, after his two years of service were completed, during the time of the Second Intifada. Violent outbreaks were everywhere, including blown-up school buses, and other attacks. It wasn't some headline about a distant city, it was happening in his own country, and he knew that he could be a victim.
On the surface, that certainly could justify the narrative he'd been told... that Palestinians were the enemy, that he and everyone he knew and loved was in danger. But, in Avner, for whatever reason, it also made him curious. **Why would these people take life, risk their own lives, risk imprisonment, risk crackdown, risk everything? What were they fighting for; what was motivating them?**
Those inquiries brought him, eventually, to meet some Palestinians directly - in his late 20s, for the first time in his life. He'd started to learn Arabic by that time, and could speak with them directly. **He heard their stories of oppression, displacement, occupation, violence, separation from loved ones and homes and land.**
And he listened. And he recognized, in their stories, the inverse of everything he'd been taught. What it was like to live on the other side. Even people who lived fifteen minutes away from his home - but had a completely unrecognizable experience of life.
As they shared their life stories, he came to understand that the system of occupation that was oppressing them -- very obviously -- was **his**. It was the uniform he wore, the military he served in, during his one month a year of reservist duty. It was the language he had been raised in and spoken from childhood. It was the architecture of justification that he'd been sold, every day of his life.
He realized, then, that **this occupation was his.** This violence, this suffering, **this oppression belonged to him** **too** , not just the settlers - he was part of it.
> _And he wanted nothing to do with it._
It turned out, he was not the only one feeling this way. Others in his unit were also ready to reject the occupation and refuse their obligation of military service.
They banded together and did so, publicly. Soldiers in other units joined in. There was a big press hullaballoo for awhile in the late '90s, covering these "refuseniks," as they were called.
Avner and his compatriots were fired from their jobs... and then, the hubbub died down. And they were left wondering, _well, what next? We refused out loud, ok, that 's done, we can't do it twice, that would be meaningless...what do we do now?_
It was at that time that, through connections, that a group of Palestinians reached out to them. Several members of the group had already spent time in Israeli jails for their role in the armed resistance. They were curious - they wanted to know more about these Israelis who refused to perpetrate violence and occupation. There was no further agenda.
Avner and his friends were confused, and cautious. _What if it was a trap? What if they were lured to the Palestinian side of the city under the promise of peace, then killed?_ But they went anyway. And Avner became quite emotional describing that meeting.
A circle of perhaps twenty, mostly men. Palestinians and Israelis both. Armed resistance, and former soldiers. Meeting without weapons, as human beings. _**Imagine**_.
At first, it was awkward; no one knew quite where to begin. Then one of the Israelis, for whatever reason, started talking. Telling his story, about his upbringing, his childhood, his education - how he came to be in the Army, and how he came to refuse military service.
Then a Palestinian spoke, telling the story of his family's dispossession, the violence against his relatives and himself, the militarized oppression of their daily lives, and how he came to fight back, and why. Then another Israeli. Then another Palestinian.
For hours, they talked with one another, and Avner took his turn to share his story, but also listened, and took it all in. And he began to see, in that moment, as the stories of violence and terror piled higher and higher, one on top of another... h**ow intensely and profoundly they had all been shaped by, and raised for, violence.**
> And how much humanity they shared.
He realized that they had all been brought up to be able, if not willing, at least able, to kill other human beings, complete strangers. He saw that these people, siting across from one another, if they had met at another time and place, he knew he himself could have killed any of them, and they could have killed him. _He described that moment as deeply confusing._
From then on, little by little, **solidarity and friendship began to grow.** Until eventually, they were organizing together, attending protests together, getting attacked together, traveling together, to share their stories.
Later in the afternoon, Avner said that "**Most people think of Israelis as evil. We 're not evil people. We're accustomed to power, and accustomed to abusing it with impunity, and it's scary to give some of that power away."**
Then he said, "My country, Israel, has become a source of darkness in the world. I am trying, we are trying, to shed light on it. Imagine, the benefit that could have on this country, on America, if Israeli society were to give light, instead of darkness. **If I, who was raised inside this, if I can transform ....anyone can."**
The entire time Avner spoke, he had been sitting on the carpet, leaning against the wall, in a circle with his compatriots and all the attendees. He was sitting comfortably close to his good friend and brother [Jamil](https://substack.com/redirect/eacda02b-3cf0-45a2-ac75-c0913c7593f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and the two hugged often, and patted one another's knees and leaned on each others' shoulders with obvious brotherhood and affection.
Jamil is Palestinian, and Avner spoke about the difference between their lives with bewildered clarity. He, an Israeli Jew, had status, privilege, economic opportunity, protection, power, freedom to travel, and so much more. Jamil -- who, clearly, he considered not just an equal but a beloved brother -- had none of that. Jamil had been told from birth that he had **no power, no dignity, and no rights** in the system of rule that he was controlled by, and subjected to.
Watching the two men joke, embrace, and grieve together, it was clear that such arbitrary superiority and inferiority was not just unfair, but obscene, and both of them knew it.
