[Jamil](https://substack.com/redirect/eacda02b-3cf0-45a2-ac75-c0913c7593f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) went last. He spoke only Arabic, so Mae translated for him, a few sentences at a time. He is a middle-aged Palestinian man, olive skin, black hair, strong and sturdy build, a quiet demeanor. He was reluctant to take much time.
He began, first, by telling us that he was a Muslim, and **as a Muslim, his faith was not complete unless he recognized, honored, and loved both the Christian faith and the Jewish faith**. As a Muslim, he was instructed by his Creator in the Quran to honor both the Gospel and the Torah, Jesus and Moses and Abraham and all the other prophets, just as he honored Muhammad and the Quran.
He told us that in his understanding, and clearly derived from the plain text of the Quran, _anyone who calls themselves Muslim who does not also honor Christianity and Judaism, their faith as a Muslim is not complete._
He told us about his mother, who taught him that there were good Jews and bad Jews, good Muslims and bad Muslims, and **there was no categorical distinction between religions that could be made.** Character was everything.
He described his gratitude for their past several days, visiting and speaking at a synagogue, then a church, and now here - these peaceful, multicultural communities of different faiths welcoming them. He said that he hoped we would learn to work together, our city's faith communities, not separately or in competition and certainly not in enmity, but together for peace. He thanked us all for being there.
Eventually, with gentle encouragement from the moderator, he told us his story.
Jamil was born in a refugee camp. His mother was displaced during the Nakba (the mass, violent expulsion of the Palestinians from their homes in 1948 that cleared the way for the settlement of Israel) at the age of two. She never had the chance to get an education, but from her, he said, he has learned so much wisdom in life.
By the time he was 20, his two older brothers were already imprisoned by Israel. In the refugee camp -- which was supposed to be a temporary stopgap, but had become an intergenerational home -- they lived under military occupation at every turn. Every part of their lives was controlled.
One time -- his younger brother, Nasser, 14 years old. Went out to go to their uncle's home, about fifty meters down the street. Israeli soldiers happened to be coming down the street at that moment. Young Nasser, understandably enough, panicked, turned, and ran away. The soldiers chased him and shot him, then escaped.
The community, distraught, gathered and carried Nasser off to seek medical care. Jamil was told that his brother was shot in the leg. Somehow, he was transferred out of the rudimentary clinic in the refugee camp, up to an Israeli hospital. Then, he was transferred to another, specialized hospital, deeper in the city. When Jamil heard this, he knew that his brother wasn't just shot in the leg. Things were worse than that.
So he went to that hospital. In the emergency department, one of the nurses was Palestinian, from the same refugee camp, and knew him. She stopped Jamil in the lobby -- wouldn't let him proceed to his brother's side -- and called for the doctors to speak with him. She and the doctors, he said, wanted to give him a shot of something to calm him down, before telling him what was going on. That was all he needed to hear.
He refused the shot, and demanded the truth. **His brother was dead.**
He pushed past them and went into his brother's hospital room. Nasser was covered in blood. He had been shot in the shoulder, and the bullet went into his chest. It was a hollow-point bullet, the type that shatters on impact and turns into shrapnel _inside_ your flesh. It was clear that Nasser hadn't made it.
At that moment, Jamil said, he knew that he needed to reclaim his brother's body immediately, before the military arrived to take it away. He described to us, and Avner corroborated, that the military usually withheld the bodies of martyrs, those killed by the occupation. He said there are bodies still in the refrigerators that have been withheld from their families for thirty years.
In great part, it was a form of punishment to the families: in Islamic culture, burying the dead is a profound expression of dignity, honor, and love. Depriving the families of that rite for their loved ones is a form of emotional and spiritual torture.
There were pragmatic consequences as well. Funerals were community affairs, especially when the deceased had been killed by the occupation. And usually, after the funeral, the shared grief rose up into a protest.
Avner added, without excusing it, that Israel initially withheld the bodies as a way of "keeping the peace" \- that is, preventing those demonstrations. Often, access to the bodies of their beloved dead was weaponized, as in, "_You can have the body, on the condition that you make sure that there 's no protest among the people after the funeral."_
Another time, years later, Jamil told us, there was an explosion targeting a school bus, full of Israeli children on their way to school. When he came home that day, his brothers were watching the news, but his mother was sitting off by herself, clearly distraught. He went to her, wanting to ease her pain.
> _He said to her, "They were just Israeli kids, mom, why are you crying?"_
She said to him then, "Every mother of every one of those children is right now feeling the same suffering I felt when they killed Nasser. And no one should ever have to go through that. **Christian, Jewish, Muslim, a mother is a mother. We all suffer the same for our kids.** Blood comes in only one color, there is no difference."
That day, he told us, he began to see the bigger picture - and to see it from multiple perspectives.
We did not hear from him today the full story of how he came to join Combatants for Peace, or the origins of his clearly profound brotherhood with Avner. But he spoke with deep affection and respect for his Israeli brother, they travel together, they face opposition together, and they work to dismantle the system that oppressed one of them and falsely exalted the other, together.

During the discussion afterward, at one point, there was a loud sound from upstairs in the mosque. The imam was preparing to give the call to prayer, and was tapping the microphone to test the sound system. The intermittent thudding echoed loudly through the speakers around and above us.
It brings tears to my eyes to remember it. **Mae visibly shrank, looking fearfully upward. I could sense, almost palpably, the shift in her awareness, from the wisdom, grace, and calm, articulate strength that she 'd shown all afternoon, to a vulnerable, helpless, and wordless fear.**
The mic test sounded, in that basement gathering room, like bombardment. It sounded like mortars falling, and **you could see in her face that she had lived through warfare, and devastation, and rubble and screams and death.** My heart ached for her, and tears sprang up. Sweet heart...
Her, and countless, countless, countless others, in Palestine and the world over...
> _**What are we doing to each other?**_
When she heard the azan, the call to prayer, begin, she visibly relaxed with understanding, and was able to return her attention to us in the room. With a sad smile, she acknowledged what trauma had done to her.

Earlier, Avner had told us:
"Our slogan is, **' There is another way.' Because most Israelis have never heard that.** Never seen it demonstrated. Israelis are told, our whole lives, that there is no other way, this is the only way, **it 's kill or be killed.** And if someone truly believes that, then most of the time, they'll learn to kill. For survival, we believe - for our loved ones. This is how they train us for violence. It's how they teach us to continue the system of occupation and oppression."
"But there is another way. Us here, together, today, we're living proof. And we do our best to be an embodiment of that peace, a demonstration of togetherness, so people don't just hear intellectually that it's possible, they see it and feel it here, with us."
"We encourage you, not just to talk about this, but to do something about it. Join us. Join something. Do something. Become an actor - take action, whether it seems small or big doesn't matter nearly as much as that you do it, and if at all possible, do it together. With us or with others. This is a life and death situation -- it's critically important, every day. **Do something.** That's our request to you."
Jamil added, through Mae:
> "Even in the darkest depths of despair, violence, and oppression, there is always a glimmer of hope. The candle may be tiny, but it glows so brightly and shines so far, even in the darkest tunnel.
> "I always ask myself, is it better for me, for my mother, for Nasser, for me to give in and lose myself in the dark? Or to **focus on the light, however small, and lean into that, with everything I am?** "

clean_body: They were supposed to be enemies. Raised to hate, fear, and kill one another. But encountering each other as human beings changed everything - and encountering them, is changing me. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? They were supposed to be enemies. Raised to hate, fear, and kill one another. But encountering each other as human beings changed everything - and encountering them, is changing me. | | | Sep 26 | | | | | | | | | | | | On Friday, my family and I went to the local mosque to hear three people speak. Jamil, Mae, and Avner - two Palestinians, and a former Israeli soldier. They were there as "Combatants for Peace," and I recommend . As a lifelong advocate for peace and justice for the Palestinian people, I'll admit I entered with some skepticism. After everything the IDF has done, how could this collaboration be sincere? How could this be trusted? Let's just say, I left with more grounded hope for peace that I've felt in a long time. Let me tell you what they had to say. Note, please, that this essay is my direct personal recollection of their presentation, shared as such -- not intended to be an ultimate, perfect, or formally approved distillation of their life stories. I fully expect that some details are incorrect; but I have reproduced the content and spirit of their messages to the best of my ability. | | ---|---|--- Mae spoke first. She is a Palestinian woman, perhaps sixty, with wide and gentle eyes, short grey hair, and a clear gaze. She started by telling us how she grew up in Bethlehem - in the occupied West Bank - before the occupation was severe. When she was small, she could walk fifteen minutes to the Dome of the Rock - or run twenty minutes to Al Aqsa. Jerusalem was open to everyone, and she spoke with deep feeling about how sacred that was -- everyone, of all faiths, shared in the holidays, met international travelers who came to Jerusalem from all over the world. Palestinian, Israeli, Muslim, Christian, Jew, the city was open to all. Only later on, did the restrictions come into place. One of her parents had a blue card, the other a green card. That means, in the pseudo apartheid system of Israeli civil society, that as the restrictions grew worse, eventually her mother and father could not live together. (Later, she and her husband, also, could not live in the same location, and she still faces restrictions in daily life on whether she can see her daughter, because of this.) When the restrictions came down, now suddenly she couldn't take a sunny afternoon run to the third-holiest place in Islam. She couldn't go to visit her family, who lived fifteen minutes' walk away, in the Old City. The restriction, division, and military oppression landed on her and her family directly. Naturally, she resisted. She was angry, and hurting, and who wouldn't be? She threw rocks. She became active in the resistance. Fighting consumed her, for quite some time, until one day her mother asked her, "Habibi (dear one), who are you going to kill to free Jerusalem? " She said, "Mama, it is not in my heart to kill anyone, I'm just trying to fight for freedom peace." Her mother admonished her, and said "Darling, when your goals do not match your actions, it does not matter what your goals are. Your actions are what you are creating, and right now, you are creating violence. If you truly want to build peace, then go get an education, become a therapist, learn about trauma, and come back and be a counselor to us, to the Palestinians. Help our people with this pain; help build a better way." So she did. She found a way to leave Palestine, and studied trauma, and came back a practicing counselor. She married a man who had an Israeli card, whereas she had a Palestinian one, which prevented them from living together under the Israeli system of occupation. It was in seeking a way to live with her husband that she first learned about shared communities, where Palestinians and Israelis have found ways to live together. She told us that her first visit to one of those communities, was her first time ever encountering and speaking with a normal Jewish Israeli person, who was not in uniform and not actively exerting military force over her and her people. From those early conversations, which helped her see the shared humanity of both communities, she began to understand that they are "cousins." Truly, she said. She told us that no one knows the Israelis better than the Palestinians - their home life, their food, their culture, their ways of thinking - and, that the Israelis know her better than any other people on earth. She began to see that togetherness was the antidote, and that the real enemy was not each other, but the system that told them they must hate and fear each other. Later in the afternoon, she spoke about how that togetherness is the strongest defensive and creative power they possess. When she travels internationally with her Jewish Israeli brothers and sisters in Combatants for Peace, what is anyone going to say at any border? What charge of antisemitism could ever be made to stick? She's not fighting anyone. She doesn't hate anyone. They're together, now, working and organizing and protesting and sharing their stories and striving, together, against the system that imposes war, violence, and separation -- striving for peace. | | ---|---|--- Mae, whose profile I could not find on Combatants for Peace's website, making friends with my husband and our daughter, whose name "Salma" means peace. Then, Avner spoke. Avner is 50 years old - he was born in 1976, in an Israeli kibbutz. He described a collective, socialist, agricultural upbringing, with apparent fondness. His father was a pacifist in his civilian life - and, specifically, opposed the occupation. An Israeli father in a Kibbutz, opposing the occupation of Palestine. As Avner described it, his father, and he, initially blamed the occupation on "the settlers," not identifying any role in it themselves. But... as an adult Israeli man, his father was also a reservist in the IDF. They all were. One month per year, his father was a soldier in uniform, obeying orders, carrying out military missions in service to the state of Israel. This contradiction was accepted with a shrug. Of course you were going to serve in the Army, everyone did, everyone had to, and you carried out the mission you were assigned -- what else were you going to do? Avner and his friends grew up knowing, without question, that at the age of 18 they would go off to the Army. And they did. Avner was honest about describing his enthusiasm at that age, and his idiocy, and his ignorance -- he became part of a well-known commando unit, and yes it was about patriotism and service and all of that, but it was also good with the girls. He told us that his unit was not assigned to carry out the dirty work of occupation, so even after his mandatory two years, he did not really know the extent of the military occupation that Palestinians were living under. He had been told, relentlessly, from a young age, that he and his family were in danger, and their military was protecting them. He had never , in his life, met or spoken with a Palestinian. Until, after his two years of service were completed, during the time of the Second Intifada. Violent outbreaks were everywhere, including blown-up school buses, and other attacks. It wasn't some headline about a distant city, it was happening in his own country, and he knew that he could be a victim. On the surface, that certainly could justify the narrative he'd been told... that Palestinians were the enemy, that he and everyone he knew and loved was in danger. But, in Avner, for whatever reason, it also made him curious. Why would these people take life, risk their own lives, risk imprisonment, risk crackdown, risk everything? What were they fighting for; what was motivating them? Those inquiries brought him, eventually, to meet some Palestinians directly - in his late 20s, for the first time in his life. He'd started to learn Arabic by that time, and could speak with them directly. He heard their stories of oppression, displacement, occupation, violence, separation from loved ones and homes and land. And he listened. And he recognized, in their stories, the inverse of everything he'd been taught. What it was like to live on the other side. Even people who lived fifteen minutes away from his home - but had a completely unrecognizable experience of life. As they shared their life stories, he came to understand that the system of occupation that was oppressing them -- very obviously -- was his. It was the uniform he wore, the military he served in, during his one month a year of reservist duty. It was the language he had been raised in and spoken from childhood. It was the architecture of justification that he'd been sold, every day of his life. He realized, then, that this occupation was his. This violence, this suffering, this oppression belonged to him too , not just the settlers - he was part of it. And he wanted nothing to do with it. It turned out, he was not the only one feeling this way. Others in his unit were also ready to reject the occupation and refuse their obligation of military service. They banded together and did so, publicly. Soldiers in other units joined in. There was a big press hullaballoo for awhile in the late '90s, covering these "refuseniks," as they were called. Avner and his compatriots were fired from their jobs... and then, the hubbub died down. And they were left wondering, well, what next? We refused out loud, ok, that 's done, we can't do it twice, that would be meaningless...what do we do now? It was at that time that, through connections, that a group of Palestinians reached out to them. Several members of the group had already spent time in Israeli jails for their role in the armed resistance. They were curious - they wanted to know more about these Israelis who refused to perpetrate violence and occupation. There was no further agenda. Avner and his friends were confused, and cautious. What if it was a trap? What if they were lured to the Palestinian side of the city under the promise of peace, then killed? But they went anyway. And Avner became quite emotional describing that meeting. A circle of perhaps twenty, mostly men. Palestinians and Israelis both. Armed resistance, and former soldiers. Meeting without weapons, as human beings. Imagine. At first, it was awkward; no one knew quite where to begin. Then one of the Israelis, for whatever reason, started talking. Telling his story, about his upbringing, his childhood, his education - how he came to be in the Army, and how he came to refuse military service. Then a Palestinian spoke, telling the story of his family's dispossession, the violence against his relatives and himself, the militarized oppression of their daily lives, and how he came to fight back, and why. Then another Israeli. Then another Palestinian. For hours, they talked with one another, and Avner took his turn to share his story, but also listened, and took it all in. And he began to see, in that moment, as the stories of violence and terror piled higher and higher, one on top of another... how intensely and profoundly they had all been shaped by, and raised for, violence. And how much humanity they shared. He realized that they had all been brought up to be able, if not willing, at least able, to kill other human beings, complete strangers. He saw that these people, siting across from one another, if they had met at another time and place, he knew he himself could have killed any of them, and they could have killed him. He described that moment as deeply confusing. From then on, little by little, solidarity and friendship began to grow. Until eventually, they were organizing together, attending protests together, getting attacked together, traveling together, to share their stories. Later in the afternoon, Avner said that "Most people think of Israelis as evil. We 're not evil people. We're accustomed to power, and accustomed to abusing it with impunity, and it's scary to give some of that power away." Then he said, "My country, Israel, has become a source of darkness in the world. I am trying, we are trying, to shed light on it. Imagine, the benefit that could have on this country, on America, if Israeli society were to give light, instead of darkness. If I, who was raised inside this, if I can transform ....anyone can." The entire time Avner spoke, he had been sitting on the carpet, leaning against the wall, in a circle with his compatriots and all the attendees. He was sitting comfortably close to his good friend and brother , and the two hugged often, and patted one another's knees and leaned on each others' shoulders with obvious brotherhood and affection. Jamil is Palestinian, and Avner spoke about the difference between their lives with bewildered clarity. He, an Israeli Jew, had status, privilege, economic opportunity, protection, power, freedom to travel, and so much more. Jamil -- who, clearly, he considered not just an equal but a beloved brother -- had none of that. Jamil had been told from birth that he had no power, no dignity, and no rights in the system of rule that he was controlled by, and subjected to. Watching the two men joke, embrace, and grieve together, it was clear that such arbitrary superiority and inferiority was not just unfair, but obscene, and both of them knew it. | | ---|---|--- Avner and Jamil, knees touching, sitting together the whole time. went last. He spoke only Arabic, so Mae translated for him, a few sentences at a time. He is a middle-aged Palestinian man, olive skin, black hair, strong and sturdy build, a quiet demeanor. He was reluctant to take much time. He began, first, by telling us that he was a Muslim, and as a Muslim, his faith was not complete unless he recognized, honored, and loved both the Christian faith and the Jewish faith. As a Muslim, he was instructed by his Creator in the Quran to honor both the Gospel and the Torah, Jesus and Moses and Abraham and all the other prophets, just as he honored Muhammad and the Quran. He told us that in his understanding, and clearly derived from the plain text of the Quran, anyone who calls themselves Muslim who does not also honor Christianity and Judaism, their faith as a Muslim is not complete. He told us about his mother, who taught him that there were good Jews and bad Jews, good Muslims and bad Muslims, and there was no categorical distinction between religions that could be made. Character was everything. He described his gratitude for their past several days, visiting and speaking at a synagogue, then a church, and now here - these peaceful, multicultural communities of different faiths welcoming them. He said that he hoped we would learn to work together, our city's faith communities, not separately or in competition and certainly not in enmity, but together for peace. He thanked us all for being there. Eventually, with gentle encouragement from the moderator, he told us his story. Jamil was born in a refugee camp. His mother was displaced during the Nakba (the mass, violent expulsion of the Palestinians from their homes in 1948 that cleared the way for the settlement of Israel) at the age of two. She never had the chance to get an education, but from her, he said, he has learned so much wisdom in life. By the time he was 20, his two older brothers were already imprisoned by Israel. In the refugee camp -- which was supposed to be a temporary stopgap, but had become an intergenerational home -- they lived under military occupation at every turn. Every part of their lives was controlled. One time -- his younger brother, Nasser, 14 years old. Went out to go to their uncle's home, about fifty meters down the street. Israeli soldiers happened to be coming down the street at that moment. Young Nasser, understandably enough, panicked, turned, and ran away. The soldiers chased him and shot him, then escaped. The community, distraught, gathered and carried Nasser off to seek medical care. Jamil was told that his brother was shot in the leg. Somehow, he was transferred out of the rudimentary clinic in the refugee camp, up to an Israeli hospital. Then, he was transferred to another, specialized hospital, deeper in the city. When Jamil heard this, he knew that his brother wasn't just shot in the leg. Things were worse than that. So he went to that hospital. In the emergency department, one of the nurses was Palestinian, from the same refugee camp, and knew him. She stopped Jamil in the lobby -- wouldn't let him proceed to his brother's side -- and called for the doctors to speak with him. She and the doctors, he said, wanted to give him a shot of something to calm him down, before telling him what was going on. That was all he needed to hear. He refused the shot, and demanded the truth. His brother was dead. He pushed past them and went into his brother's hospital room. Nasser was covered in blood. He had been shot in the shoulder, and the bullet went into his chest. It was a hollow-point bullet, the type that shatters on impact and turns into shrapnel inside your flesh. It was clear that Nasser hadn't made it. At that moment, Jamil said, he knew that he needed to reclaim his brother's body immediately, before the military arrived to take it away. He described to us, and Avner corroborated, that the military usually withheld the bodies of martyrs, those killed by the occupation. He said there are bodies still in the refrigerators that have been withheld from their families for thirty years. In great part, it was a form of punishment to the families: in Islamic culture, burying the dead is a profound expression of dignity, honor, and love. Depriving the families of that rite for their loved ones is a form of emotional and spiritual torture. There were pragmatic consequences as well. Funerals were community affairs, especially when the deceased had been killed by the occupation. And usually, after the funeral, the shared grief rose up into a protest. Avner added, without excusing it, that Israel initially withheld the bodies as a way of "keeping the peace" \- that is, preventing those demonstrations. Often, access to the bodies of their beloved dead was weaponized, as in, "You can have the body, on the condition that you make sure that there 's no protest among the people after the funeral." Another time, years later, Jamil told us, there was an explosion targeting a school bus, full of Israeli children on their way to school. When he came home that day, his brothers were watching the news, but his mother was sitting off by herself, clearly distraught. He went to her, wanting to ease her pain. He said to her, "They were just Israeli kids, mom, why are you crying?" She said to him then, "Every mother of every one of those children is right now feeling the same suffering I felt when they killed Nasser. And no one should ever have to go through that. Christian, Jewish, Muslim, a mother is a mother. We all suffer the same for our kids. Blood comes in only one color, there is no difference." That day, he told us, he began to see the bigger picture - and to see it from multiple perspectives. We did not hear from him today the full story of how he came to join Combatants for Peace, or the origins of his clearly profound brotherhood with Avner. But he spoke with deep affection and respect for his Israeli brother, they travel together, they face opposition together, and they work to dismantle the system that oppressed one of them and falsely exalted the other, together. | | ---|---|--- Attendees listening deeply. During the discussion afterward, at one point, there was a loud sound from upstairs in the mosque. The imam was preparing to give the call to prayer, and was tapping the microphone to test the sound system. The intermittent thudding echoed loudly through the speakers around and above us. It brings tears to my eyes to remember it. Mae visibly shrank, looking fearfully upward. I could sense, almost palpably, the shift in her awareness, from the wisdom, grace, and calm, articulate strength that she 'd shown all afternoon, to a vulnerable, helpless, and wordless fear. The mic test sounded, in that basement gathering room, like bombardment. It sounded like mortars falling, and you could see in her face that she had lived through warfare, and devastation, and rubble and screams and death. My heart ached for her, and tears sprang up. Sweet heart... Her, and countless, countless, countless others, in Palestine and the world over... What are we doing to each other? When she heard the azan, the call to prayer, begin, she visibly relaxed with understanding, and was able to return her attention to us in the room. With a sad smile, she acknowledged what trauma had done to her. | | ---|---|--- Mae, at a stronger moment, earlier in the afternoon. I do not know what to say, about that, except that I live in a country where our collective money is spent paying for those bombs, at grotesque markups, for private profit, recycled into political corruption to keep those bombs dropping and the profits flowing. Those mortars that terrorized her and killed who knows how many of her family, friends, neighbors, relatives' children... American taxpayers bought them. Paid for them. Footed the bill. And our so-called "Representatives" signed off on it, supposedly acting in our interests, and on our behalf. To put it bluntly: Fuck. This. Over snacks, after the gathering, I spoke with Nicole, who organized this tour and works on behalf of Combatants for Peace here in America. I asked her how these three people are treated in Israeli society. That depends, she answered. Yes, their offices and meeting places have been attacked. Yes, when they attend protests, people often don't want them there. Yes, she said, it's difficult. But 'we also fundraise in Israel, and we do find support there.' " Are there Israelis who support them? Definitely. Yes." | | ---|---|--- Nicole, making friends with my son, "Adil," whose name means Justice. Earlier, Avner had told us: "Our slogan is, ' There is another way.' Because most Israelis have never heard that. Never seen it demonstrated. Israelis are told, our whole lives, that there is no other way, this is the only way, it 's kill or be killed. And if someone truly believes that, then most of the time, they'll learn to kill. For survival, we believe - for our loved ones. This is how they train us for violence. It's how they teach us to continue the system of occupation and oppression." "But there is another way. Us here, together, today, we're living proof. And we do our best to be an embodiment of that peace, a demonstration of togetherness, so people don't just hear intellectually that it's possible, they see it and feel it here, with us." "We encourage you, not just to talk about this, but to do something about it. Join us. Join something. Do something. Become an actor - take action, whether it seems small or big doesn't matter nearly as much as that you do it, and if at all possible, do it together. With us or with others. This is a life and death situation -- it's critically important, every day. Do something. That's our request to you." Jamil added, through Mae: "Even in the darkest depths of despair, violence, and oppression, there is always a glimmer of hope. The candle may be tiny, but it glows so brightly and shines so far, even in the darkest tunnel. "I always ask myself, is it better for me, for my mother, for Nasser, for me to give in and lose myself in the dark? Or to focus on the light, however small, and lean into that, with everything I am? " | | ---|---|--- " For there is always light, if only we're brave enough to see it -- if only we're brave enough to be it. Congresswoman Delia Ramirez (D-IL) announced her plan to eliminate the Department of Homeland Security in a deliberate effort to end immigration enforcement by getting rid of Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection.
Ramirez explained her bill, The Reimagining Safety Act, is necessary because "DHS must be dismantled, piece by piece, and something new - a system that honors our rights, our dignity, and our humanity - must be built" and the bill "will dismantle DHS and create a new human- and community-centered federal department: The Department of Community Safety to promote collective care and well-being."
During her press conference about the bill, Ramirez addressed the attendees in English and Spanish.

In the Spanish portion of her event, she said Congress must get rid of DHS so "our people will no longer have to live in fear of an unjust system" and so that immigration is not handled by an agency that likes to label immigrants as terrorists.
Ramirez's comments outlining her plan drew the most backlash, especially the part where she referred to illegal immigrants as "our people" in Spanish.
That phrasing is no accident. Far-left types like Ramirez are a prime example as to how insane our political system has become. Beyond her crazy idea to get rid of DHS to end immigration enforcement, Ramirez's family history emphasizes the importance of having sound national policy.

Ramirez is, by her own admission, a "proud anchor baby" since her mother arrived in the United States when she was pregnant after leaving Guatemala. The Congresswoman infamously declared she is more proud to be a Guatemalan than an American last year during a far-left conference in Mexico City.
Any time she has a chance to profess loyalty, she does so to people who are not American. Even before this bill's announcement, Ramirez has hammered the absurd message of "DHS is still the single greatest threat to our communities."
Ramirez has also come to the defense of fellow Democrat LaMonica McIver, who is in a court battle after being caught on camera assaulting federal law enforcement outside of an ICE facility in New Jersey last year.

"Rep McIver did her job, conducted oversight, and protected her constituents and our communities. Today's decision from the Third Circuit is an attack on Congressional oversight. I stand with Rep McIver. We will continue to fight for our communities, defend our rights, and hold this authoritarian administration accountable. The fight is not over!" said Ramirez.
It should be no surprise that people like Ramirez have no love or loyalty to the United States and seek to undermine it from their positions of power. It is why the midterms are so important.
Democrats have made no attempt to hide their plans should they gain control of Congress. All of the real gains made by the Trump administration will grind to a halt because Democrats will be hard at work for their people, and it's not Americans.
**Honor and courage.**

Fellow Conservative: Texas is about to decide the fate of the Senate majority — and if we lose it, we won't just lose a seat. We'll hand Democrats their first statewide win in Texas since 1994, and the earthquake will be felt by Americans across the country. First, let's be clear about how we got here. The Republican establishment in DC spent over $150 million — the most expensive Senate primary in American history — trying to stop Ken Paxton from becoming the nominee. _They lost._ Paxton defeated Sen. John Cornyn by nearly 30 points. But the damage was done, and now Democrat James Talarico is within striking distance of flipping the seat. You'd think Cornyn would be all-in to stop him from turning Texas blue. Nope. Instead, he's trashing Paxton as lazy and a poor campaigner, while telling reporters the party shouldn't spend another dime on his race because of limited resources. That's rich. **Even worse, Cornyn is working with former President George W. Bush to pull money out of Texas to fund moderate Senate candidates in other states — many of whom are far bigger underdogs than Paxton.** With friends like these, who needs enemies?

Ken Paxton has spent over a decade as Texas Attorney General doing what the GOP establishment only talks about. He sued the Biden administration more than any other AG in the country — on the border, on illegal mandates, on federal overreach — and won. While career politicians in Washington cut deals, Paxton has been on the front lines of the fight against the open-borders agenda. President Trump didn't endorse him as an afterthought — he called Paxton a "true MAGA warrior" because Paxton has earned it. That's exactly why the establishment tried to kill his campaign before it started and why they're throwing a temper tantrum now. A real fighter in the Senate threatens the comfortable do-nothing environment they've built in DC. They'd rather have an empty suit who plays along with their empty promises and endless excuses than a conservative who delivers. **Make no mistake: John Cornyn and the GOP establishment are working against Paxton because they want Texas to lose. They need it to lose, so they can point at the wreckage and say, _"See? Only RINOs can win."_ It's a self-fulfilling prophecy.** They know the game. Give conservative voters a choice between a Democrat and a RINO, and we'll hold our nose and vote RINO. But give us a choice between a Democrat and a real conservative, and the establishment would rather watch us lose than let us win on our own terms. Even worse, Cornyn is working with former President George W. Bush to pull money out of Texas to fund moderate Senate candidates in other states — many of whom are far bigger underdogs than Paxton. With friends like these, who needs enemies? Ken Paxton has spent over a decade as Texas Attorney General doing what the GOP establishment only talks about. He sued the Biden administration more than any other AG in the country — on the border, on illegal mandates, on federal overreach — and won. While career politicians in Washington cut deals, Paxton has been on the front lines of the fight against the open-borders agenda. President Trump didn't endorse him as an afterthought — he called Paxton a "true MAGA warrior" because Paxton has earned it. That's exactly why the establishment tried to kill his campaign before it started and why they're throwing a temper tantrum now. A real fighter in the Senate threatens the comfortable do-nothing environment they've built in DC. They'd rather have an empty suit who plays along with their empty promises and endless excuses than a conservative who delivers. Make no mistake: John Cornyn and the GOP establishment are working against Paxton because they want Texas to lose. They need it to lose, so they can point at the wreckage and say, "See? Only RINOs can win." It's a self-fulfilling prophecy. They know the game. Give conservative voters a choice between a Democrat and a RINO, and we'll hold our nose and vote RINO. But give us a choice between a Democrat and a real conservative, and the establishment would rather watch us lose than let us win on our own terms. It was never about winning a majority; it was about maintaining their control over the party. Senate Conservatives Fund exists for exactly this fight — to back conservative candidates in the races the party committees have already written off, when the committees would rather protect their own than protect the country. You can donate to SCF to support our independent efforts to elect Ken Paxton, and you can contribute directly to his campaign. It's the best way to help conservatives win in Texas. We are running out of time, so please take action before it's too late. to help Ken Paxton finish this fight — and send the establishment a message they won't forget: their days of picking our nominees for us are over. The future of the Republican Party belongs to conservatives, and we're sending John Cornyn's replacement to Washington. A Maine group-home operator that collected approximately $27.8 million in MaineCare payments over five years is facing a state-ordered funding cutoff after inspectors found a medically fragile resident left unattended, failures to follow feeding orders and a home without hot water.
Quality Care Access (QCA) and a second company, We Care Residential Services, face an Oct. 13 funding deadline after the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) refused to issue them provisional licenses.
Notably, the state's move to suspend payments to QCA comes just weeks after the Maine Wire's Jon Fetherston published a harrowing video report featuring whistleblower testimony about the company and an interview with a neglected patient of the company.

State and federal payment records show that the company, which lists the deceased Justin Nsenga as its authorized official on provider records, collected more than $27.8 million in taxpayer cash before the Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) took action. Maine Secretary of State records list [Jovin Bayingana](https://substack.com/redirect/4e41f330-e888-4e31-9d80-498d8ff2aec6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as the founder of the company. According to his LinkedIn account, Bayingana worked at DHHS from August 2012 to October 2021.
QCA's records identify Nsenga, Bayingana, Yves Mpundu, Rapha Nsenga and attorney Julien D. Guerard as representatives for the provider.
According to an analysis of federal provider payment data, Quality Care Access charged more per patient than any adult autism residential care operator in the country. Federal records show QCA received nearly $40,000 per month for every disabled adult living in their homes.
Despite the extreme volume of taxpayer cash flowing into the organization, an ex-employee compared the existence of disabled adults in their care to that of "prisoners."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/8010fe41-9e5c-440e-8212-878c4b2a2f32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"It was like they were prisoners in their own home," the former employee told the Maine Wire.
During Fetherston's investigation into Quality Care Access, the company filed a no trespass order against him after he visited one of the houses where the state now says disabled adults were being neglected. Video recorded at the time shows that Fetherston was voluntarily invited into the house by non-English speaking staff and the client voluntarily consented to an interview -- but wanted to be interviewed outside the home where the staffers wouldn't be able to hear.
At QCA's **1** 8 Wood Ave., Saco, house, inspectors visiting in May found a medically fragile resident left unattended despite needing total staff support. The DHHS notice also cites malnutrition, failures to follow feeding orders, medication problems and inadequate nursing oversight.
At QCA's 420 Flag Pond Road house in Saco, DHHS cited failures involving physician orders, CPAP treatment and medication administration, along with a lack of hot water and failures to report abuse, neglect or exploitation. The assessed owner is Marie G. Mukarugema, who bought the property in October 2021 for $410,000.
QCA also manages homes at Lewis Road, Westbrook, a two-family property owned by Jacques Kubwimana and Ange Abaribeza.
Like with Paradise Residential Care, the autism firm run by Jocelyne Ininahazwe that was shuttered in March, QCA appears to utilize the same corporate structure wherein associates own the properties that are then rented to the Medicaid agency for lucrative fees.
According to federal records, We Care Residential Services' authorized official is Gatimbirizo Daniel Mucyo; the registered agent on the corporate filing is Francois N. Rukumbuzi. The company is registered at 120 Blue Spruce Farm Road, Westbrook.
DHHS sent its July 23 refusal notice to Mucyo at P.O. Box 398, Westbrook.
We Care's refusal letter describes a resident's death at 15 Autumn Lane, Brewer. A resident with a known eating disorder and history of choking ate alone without supervision Sept. 15, 2024, was found unresponsive and could not be resuscitated, according to DHHS.
Two days earlier, two workers allegedly slapped a resident who refused to get out of a car. The department said police arrested the workers; the letter does not give their names or the outcome of any criminal case.
According to police records reviewed by the Maine Wire, the We Care employee who called the police after the fatal choking was Jonathan Nduwayo. Also present at the home were Modest Irakiza and Moses Tumusiime.
In the police report, one responding officer wrote: "It should be noted that I contacted Adult Protective Services regarding [the surviving patient's] well-being. I do not feel staff possess the skills to care for disabled individuals as they let [the deceased.] who had a known eating disorder, eat by himself in his bedroom."
"It should be noted that I contacted Adult Protective Services regarding [the surviving patient's] well-being. I do not feel staff possess the skills to care for disabled individuals as they let [the deceased.] who had a known eating disorder, eat by himself in his bedroom."
Brewer's fiscal 2027 tax commitment book lists Francois Rukumbuzi and Esperance Ndutira as the property's owners.
DHHS also cited failures at 51 Winston Way, New Gloucester, including a resident leaving while staff slept, and at 13 Mount Desert Drive, Bangor, including medication administration by uncertified workers. The current assessed owners are 21 Leighton LLC and Lilyhills LLC, respectively. The New Gloucester company's recorded acquisition came after the March 2024 incident described in the notice.
We Care's principal office as 123 North St., Westbrook, while its federal practice and mailing address remains 169 Mechanic St., Westbrook. The municipal owners are Morgan Rock Loehr and Nicki Mokhtari at North Street and Tharcisse Byinshi and Aimee Murekatete at Mechanic Street.
We Care received $6.26 million in MaineCare payments in 2024 and 2025, according to state and federal Medicaid payment records.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..RAKwfmc_SIocZZsAAawmXbTE5nh8_ZqJLT_e9Tl464s?)
DHHS initially set a Sept. 30 billing cutoff. The department has since extended that deadline to midnight Oct. 13, contingent on QCA and We Care helping residents move to licensed providers.
In a [June 30 letter](https://substack.com/redirect/d4d30444-f966-4d2c-a025-b5a5858c5a92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) addressed to Yves Mpundu at QCA's South Portland office, DHHS denied the company's Oct. 25, 2025, application for a provisional home and community support service agency license.
The department concluded that QCA had neither met licensing requirements nor demonstrated that it could come into compliance during a provisional licensing period.
The department cited missing or outdated care records, inadequate staff training, a lack of nursing oversight and medication discrepancies. Staff had not been adequately trained on residents' medical conditions, equipment and health needs, the letter said.
At a second Saco home, at 420 Flag Pond Road, investigators found failures involving physician orders, CPAP treatment, staffing and medication administration. The home lacked hot water, and the company failed to report abuse, neglect or exploitation to the Division of Licensing and Certification, according to the notice.
At a Lewis Road property in Westbrook, investigations in February and May found expired medications, discrepancies in medication records and a failure to promptly correct conditions that endangered a resident's safety.
The letter also cited a Feb. 26 corrective action plan from the Office of Aging and Disability Services concerning QCA's failure to provide background checks.
DHHS concluded that the company's deficiencies threatened the health and safety of the people in its care.
QCA has declined interview requests from the Maine Wire.

The Maine Wire's analysis of state payment records obtained under Maine's Freedom of Access Act put QCA's MaineCare payments at approximately $27.8 million from 2021 through 2025. The reported annual figures rose from about $1.2 million in 2021 to $7.2 million in 2025.
The suspension of payments to Quality Care Access and We Care bring the total number of MaineCare Section 21 adult autism homes shuttered pursuant to Maine Wire investigations to four.
Paradise Residential Care and Beyond Residential Care were both terminated for similar reasons in March.

Peter, For generations, pro-working-class Black leaders have helped move our country forward: fighting to expand opportunity, protect civil rights, and build a democracy that works for everyone. But too often, talented Black candidates face greater barriers to raising the resources they need to run competitive campaigns. Without sustained investment, communities can lose experienced advocates and promising new voices before they ever have the opportunity to serve. This November is all or nothing for the Left. And they're counting on patriots like you to stay home.

WIN more races. ** It's what Charlie called "the clipboard and tennis shoes" work to reach every voter. | | | Right now, in towns across this country, massive data centers are being built, and residents have no idea what's actually happening until it's too late. Here's how it works: Data center developers sign non-disclosure agreements, known as “NDAs,” with local government officials — sometimes state agencies, sometimes city councils, sometimes both. Those NDAs shroud the most basic facts a community deserves to know: how much water the facility will drain from local supplies, how much electricity it will pull from the grid, what infrastructure demands it will create, and how many taxpayer dollars are being handed over in incentives. Communities find out about all of it after the decision has already been made. By then, it's too late to ask questions, too late to push back, too late to demand a better deal. **_I think that's wrong, and I said so plainly: Americans have a right to know how these projects affect their communities._** Secrecy agreements should never be allowed to keep the public in the dark about decisions with this much impact on their water, their power bills, and their tax dollars. That's why I'm calling for a ban on NDAs between data center developers and government officials or agencies at any level, from Washington all the way down to your city hall. There is no Equal Opportunity if the people footing the bill are the last ones to find out what they're paying for. This is exactly why I founded Equal Opportunity Now: to elect leaders who believe transparency isn't optional, and who will fight to make sure decisions this consequential never get made behind closed doors again. **[Chip in $25 or $50 right now and help us put a stop to backroom deals that leave your community in the dark.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140034387/649306103/1090555623?amount=25&refcode=260926_reworkedai&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMTE1ZDI1Ny1kNmI5LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=8boM2k4xBK8ESn7ciKG5miolRr9bAWchmceUzxl2u6U=)**

Folks,
I'll always be honest with you. And these midterm elections will be the most consequential in modern history.
_Read that again._
Stopping Trump's obscene corruption and abuse. Restoring healthcare for millions. Defending our Republic and its Constitution...
_**It all hinges on regaining Congressional power this November. And it 's all going to come down to Georgia again.**_
Republicans know that if they defeat me, there is no path to a Democratic Senate majority ... and therefore no path to real accountability for the crook President.
**[So if you 're outraged by what's happening to our country -- and you're ready to fight for our Republic -- please don't wait until 2028: Rush $5 to my reelection campaign in Georgia right now.](https://substack.com/redirect/0dcd11bf-3ec0-4b65-a37f-f146edf2690c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Our task is not just to contain this president's wickedness, but to repair the deeper brokenness beneath it -- and then to advance into a new era of reform, progress, and justice.
And in that struggle, these midterm elections will be decisive.

We are 38 days away from victory. That’s only 38 days to reclaim our community, Congress, and Constitution.

Every one of the remaining 38 days is precious, because time is what campaigns can never get back. We have the momentum in this race, but we do not have much time. But we do have you!

_This race is going to come down to the wire. Every voter we reach today puts our victory closer to within reach._

Let me tell you why I believe we are going to win:

Right now, people are already furious about skyrocketing prices. They’re furious about healthcare clinics and services shutting down. And they are furious about John McGuire selling out our communities to pay back his dark money donors.

But people are also hopeful. They are excited to have a real alternative this year: a candidate who will fight for universal healthcare, higher wages, and ending foreign wars. I wouldn’t have guessed this, but the #1 thing voters – right, left and center – tell me each day is, _“Thank you! Thank you for running and giving us a chance to have real representation again.”_

"Can you say... mama?"
This is Marilyn, and if you have a young child at home, like I do, you might read that sentence in Ms. Rachel's voice (also like I do!), with an image of her pink headband and jean overalls.
For millions of children and parents like me, Ms. Rachel has been a familiar voice in the living room during the strange and exhausting early years of childhood.
Now, she's become the voice not just to, but for, millions of suffering children in America and around the globe. Powerful people are trying to silence her for it, but she's doing it anyway, because she believes it's the right thing to do. What is happening to our world that a children's YouTube star has to speak truth to power for anyone to even notice these children?
Lucas's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9sdWNhc2t1bmNlLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.jtcIGvvEojLjDCgHZHsXe3IDnbN10MrgAG0VaKVq7l8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=217568348)
I am gonna start by letting y'all know that we are not gonna get into the screen-free or screens allowed side of the debate today!
In my case, I started playing Ms. Rachel's videos for moments where I didn't have a helping hand nearby and needed to run to the restroom, or when attending to a toddler and a newborn was a little difficult to do at the same time.
Ms. Rachel became part teacher, part entertainer, part nanny, during those short stretches of time when I needed help.
Some moms turn her on when they need a few minutes to make food, to shower for the first time this week, or to be able to start a new load of laundry after living off the dryer load and running out of clothes. Let's be so for real here, who has time to fold and put away clothes when you have young children?
I think y'all get the point. People say, "we all need a village". Well, in today's day, where moms can be isolated by the many turns of this era, that village sometimes is a short Ms. Rachel video.
As moms, we tend to have high, and a lot of times unachievable, expectations for ourselves. Fellow momma out there, if you're trying your best, you are a good mom in my book.
Recently, though, I've learned that there are heavier times when moms and dads need to turn to Ms. Rachel.
In the hospital, the cancer ward, even pediatric hospice...
Sigh, I have to pause here because my little Harvey spent a terrifying two months in pediatric intensive care and it gives me extreme sadness to think that pediatric hospice has to exist and to imagine the pain the parents of those children must feel.
In these hardest situations, when we might not have the strength to to do it ourselves, parents can count on Ms. Rachel to be there by their side and talk to them with genuine joy, showing up virtually to sing to them with the biggest and warmest smile.
Recently I've learned that there is another dark place, something we don't like to talk about, or we don't like to see because it is uncomfortable, where Ms. Rachel shows up. On the other side of the world, where there is war. It is everywhere these days, and while it is hard to avoid, we nevertheless can avoid it, and we certainly do avoid looking into its details.
We are so SO incredibly lucky here in America, where war isn't in our neighborhoods and we can tune it out of our screens. We don't have to keep our children inside to keep them from being injured or killed, on a daily basis by a freaking bomb.
Parents in war zones like Ukraine and Gaza and beyond rely on Ms. Rachel in more ways than we can imagine.
Ms. Rachel discovered this horrible truth when she was alerted [that mothers were playing her videos for their children in Gaza during amputations without amnesia](https://substack.com/redirect/767bfbe4-125b-46b2-b1d8-330b6a5dfb84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Can you imagine your little children having their legs and arms cut off, and the only thing they had to numb the pain was Ms. Rachel?
If you haven't watched this video of [an American doctor describing what it is like to amputate on a little girl without amnesia](https://substack.com/redirect/a451798b-044e-4cff-9dad-2f7ab1a0e832?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and only songs at your disposal, praying that she would faint or pass out (which she never did), then you should. Because these are the horrors Americans have been ignoring and that Ms. Rachel is working to bring to light.
I sobbed in horror when I learned [the story of Rahaf](https://substack.com/redirect/2b2e98de-b2e0-4bf1-944e-b69116d68c88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a little girl no older than Harvey, my three-year-old that Ms. Rachel invited to her show. Rahaf was hit by an Israeli airstrike and [lost both her legs](https://substack.com/redirect/cc945345-0c57-4eea-b308-833e33af3650?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). She and her mom were evacuated after the attack, but not her brothers or father. Her big brothers were only seven and nine years old. The youngest of them, [Ahmed, has been injured twice now during airstrikes](https://substack.com/redirect/52904d18-1dd2-4aac-b88d-10e58b5facb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and he is still trapped in Gaza.
These children don't have a voice, most people don't know, and probably don't want to know, the things that are happening to them because they don't want their beliefs challenged. But Ms. Rachel is giving them a voice and a platform anyway.
At such young age, Rahaf understands that she is separated from her brothers. She explains how [she and her mom avoid eating while video-chatting her brothers and dad](https://substack.com/redirect/6688cdd2-0537-4859-a981-022a07edff5f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Gaza as food is very scarce there and a lot are starving.
If you're reading this and you have children, and you can move past the international politics that close so many eyes, you should understand how horrible this is. No child should have to go through these things, but so many are. And their stories are hardly being told because of politics. I'm not writing this from a political point of view. This isn't about politics. This is about humanity.
Ms. Rachel was the one who covered Rahaf's story. Even now, as I'm writing this and looking through links to add as sources so you can read more about it, it is through Ms. Rachel's posts where you get the most information.
This isn't the only dark place Ms. Rachel has brought children joy or given them a voice. She is doing it right here in America, for [children imprisoned in immigration detention centers, like Dilley ICE Detention.](https://substack.com/redirect/c85dec6e-26eb-47b8-b252-7cfbdeb338bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Organizations such as Human Rights First, RAICES, and Amnesty International have documented systemic due process violations and lasting physical and psychological harm inflicted on infants, young children, and pregnant individuals at the center. Human Rights First described it as "[unfathomably cruel and an assault on the rights, dignity, and wellbeing of children](https://substack.com/redirect/2cad710b-1eba-48f8-8c00-6b726242dd5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**".**
There, children are frightened, and in some cases separated from their parents. [Some as young as two months old are detained](https://substack.com/redirect/ff5a3e04-2478-4ca9-baf4-f04f727f7b44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [They are forced to eat food containing mold, worms, or other contaminants and dirty water.](https://substack.com/redirect/0b37618b-271a-4139-94d1-d3e6729ab3ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Some have experienced serious medical emergencies, and families have reported being denied or delays in receiving prescribed medication.
These little prisoners have counted on Ms. Rachel to be there with them and bring them joy in one of the cruelest places in America.
Rachel Accurso spoke directly with families held at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center in Texas.
And she brought their stories to Congress where politicians who claim to care about the lives of "all children" have chosen to bury their heads in the sand or look the other way out of political convenience.
Ms. Rachel walked into Washington with packets of those [children's words and artwork](https://substack.com/redirect/0fa542f7-c12e-4971-a1b0-0bc4b942d199?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). She met with congressional offices from across both isles, Democratic and Republican, and urged lawmakers to end family detention and reunite children with their parents. She ultimately set out to deliver materials to every member of Congress.
**A Platform for Children**
Ms. Rachel did not begin by trying to become a political celebrity.
She began as a mother and an educator.
According to Rachel Accurso, her son's speech delay was one of the reasons she became interested in creating media that could help children develop language. She had already taught music and had started an in-person baby-and-toddler music class. In 2019, she brought that idea to YouTube.
As a mom and aunt of children that went through speech delay, I personally experienced the powerful tools that speech therapy and speech coaching are for getting your kids to make some advancement.
Ms. Rachel's platform began as a helpful tool to mothers, then it grew.
The pandemic arrived, and millions of parents suddenly found themselves searching for ways to educate, entertain and connect with young children at home. _[Songs for Littles](https://substack.com/redirect/9dee96ec-81af-4cae-a8cc-82e499412d42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ became something much bigger than a local children's music class that was originally imagined.
By 2025, the Washington Post reported that the channel had nearly 16 million YouTube subscribers, alongside a growing presence on Netflix and elsewhere. Today, Ms. Rachel's YouTube audience is above 20 million.
If we think about it, reaching 20 million homes in a world where we are more divided than ever is, to put it simply, impressive.
20 million parents have placed their trust in her.
Public figures and influencers from different fields try to avoid getting political or controversial in any way beyond what's "acceptable" because they risk losing it all. Getting cancelled is the biggest fear of the era (Ask [Ed Sheeran](https://substack.com/redirect/ba77280c-d5de-4ebf-b32a-ebcc04e27518?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about this).
And as a teacher, Ms. Rachel probably had the easiest path to stay in her lane by just continuing to make more content for children's entertainment.
But this is where she differentiated herself.
There came a moment that she realized that with that enormous platform she had built, she had power and with that came responsibility.
She stopped thinking just as a content creator, she made the decision to ask herself a harder and braver question:
_What do I feel responsible for saying because people are listening?_
That transition is especially complicated for someone whose entire public identity was built around children. Moms, teachers, educators, nannies, we are supposed to be role models. We are supposed to be sweet, funny, happy, joyful, but never political.
Although, Ms. Rachel's advocacy did not begin with one single political issue. She has spoken publicly about early education, paid family leave, LGBTQ+ inclusion and humanitarian crises. Her advocacy around children in Gaza, in particular, has transformed the way many people understand her public role.
In 2024, [she launched a fundraiser benefiting children affected by conflict](https://substack.com/redirect/5ebc1023-68bd-44ed-b692-1f35086508c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including children in Gaza, Sudan and Ukraine. She raised $50,000 through personalized cameo videos.
She spent years telling all children that their feelings matter, their voices matter and they deserve to be heard, and when she realized that their voices didn't matter to the people in charge, she decided to do something about it.
That advocacy has brought praise, but also criticism and organized backlash. Her Gaza advocacy even led one so-called [pro-Israel organization to call for a Justice Department investigation into whether she was acting as a foreign agent](https://substack.com/redirect/05fd1c56-7c93-4f0c-954d-b7e94ad3b4c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with no factual basis.
It says a lot about our country that a woman is risking her career and platform just by giving a voice to children that most people want to ignore. And it says a lot about Ms. Rachel that she's risking it anyway, walking into the Capitol carrying the voices of children who cannot walk in themselves, and telling the story of children suffering around the globe when others choose not to.
**Rachel Accurso is here to stay**
Ms. Rachel gave Rachel Accurso a platform for political issues. And yesterday, [as Ms. Rachel and Mr. Aron release their very first album,](https://substack.com/redirect/1e9145a8-3b32-460f-bcf0-4a2e4638d94d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Rachel Accurso is louder than ever.
I am personally grateful and in awe of her growth, which is why I decided to write this Substack. Because she is an example of social responsibility. She is an example of an everyday person that doesn't hold office using her power for good beyond her own.
Congratulations, Rachel. Harvey, Lukie and I will blast your album every school drop off and pick up, and I will continue to follow your journey to bring voices to littles all over the world in full support.
Marilyn

* * *
_**by Matt Robison**_
**Toplines for the Week**
You ever watch an instant replay of a bone-crunching NFL tackle? First you see the approaching defender about to make impact. Then the ball carrier falls. Finally, you see the referee running in.
That's what the last three weeks felt like in the battle for the midterms.
Labor Day week brought indications about a fast-approaching blue-shift. Then the first batch of post-Labor Day polls arrived last week and [impact arrived](https://substack.com/redirect/54572011-0b55-457d-b432-d3bd86dbbca8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Now, this week, the media referees are running in to whistle that the GOP has been sacked.
Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

Every structural indicator this week moved toward Democrats. All of them. [Again](https://substack.com/redirect/54572011-0b55-457d-b432-d3bd86dbbca8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Poll averages moved. Individual races moved. Prediction markets moved. Race ratings moved. About the only bright spot for Republicans was the flood gates opening on their emergency money stash...and even that showed signs of panic buying. Overall, it looked like the week that the GOP went into red zone defense.
**Midterm HQ Weekly Dashboard: Week of September 21, 2026**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/44dc2705-7ecc-4746-9792-3599311bbd9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The Structural Picture**
The numbers speak for themselves. What speaks louder perhaps is this article yesterday from _The National Review_ ,[1] which opens with:
"On the menu today: Republicans like to believe they're the party that is more supportive of law enforcement, and these days they're quoting The Police when it comes to President Trump: "Don't Stand So Close to Me." GOP candidates running for office could only appear connected to a president with a high-30-something job approval rating for so long. This week, everywhere you look, Republicans are emphasizing that they want the war against Iran to end, and will do whatever it takes to bring down unleaded gasoline prices and diesel prices."
With due respect to Sting, the better song choice here would have been OneRepublic's "[It's Too Late to] Apologize." The time for Republicans to make a break was months ago, when there was still a chance to make a high-profile Trump slap-back while Congress was still in session. It could have helped, as I [wrote about in mid-August](https://substack.com/redirect/957a5d58-3ac6-4c3f-8d2f-01f7b6ec89d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) using an example from Democrats and my own painful experience as a congressional chief of staff for a Democrat who _didn 't _break from an unpopular President:
"In 2010, House Democrats sitting in districts John McCain had carried who voted _for_ the Affordable Care Act survived reelection at a rate of 11%--two out of eighteen. Those who voted _against_ it survived at a rate of 39%--nine out of twenty-three. Another piece of evidence: Nyhan, McGhee, Sides, Masket & Greene (_American Politics Research_ , 2012) estimate that the ACA vote cost yes-voting Democrats 5.8 points of vote share, and that Democrats would have held roughly 25 more seat**s** had members in competitive districts voted no."

So I have to ask: **_How much MORE should American taxpayers be expected to shoulder?_** **President Trump's new "public charge" rule would give federal immigration officers greater discretion to deny green cards and admission to immigrants who are either** _**on welfare**_**or deemed** _**likely to become dependent on taxpayer-funded public assistance**_**.** To AMAC Action, that is common sense: If someone wants to build a permanent future in America and become a citizen, taxpayers shouldn't be expected to finance it for them._They should be able to show reasonable promise that they can contribute to the economy rather than become a burden on the taxpayer._ And it is long overdue, especially in light of shocking revelations about widespread **fraud rings** in places like **Minneapolis** , where individuals of mostly Somali origin **_have defrauded the public to the tune of billions of dollars._** Yet, this hasn’t stopped Democrats from a full-force meltdown. **A coalition of 22 Democrat states, all led by New York City’s Zohran Mamdani, have filed a lawsuit to block President Trump.** But my friend, here’s what gets me:**YOU are the one who spent decades paying into the system.** You contributed to Social Security and Medicare. You paid for schools, roads, national defense, and assistance for Americans who fell on hard times.**You worked. You saved. You played by the rules.****And now you're being asked to stretch your retirement dollars further and further while Washington fights over how much more taxpayers should provide.** But why should, you, an American taxpayer, be expected to shoulder migrants draining our public resources?Instead of supporting our families and saving our hard-earned money, Democrats are emphatic about suing Trump to stop him. Once again, proving their loyalty to foreigners rather than American Citizens. _**We should be outraged that individuals on welfare can be granted citizenship in the first place.**_**The United States should not and cannot be the food pantry of the world.** Productive, taxpaying citizens are already asked to shoulder an enormous load to maintain critical infrastructure, fund welfare and entitlements for American citizens, and pay for the nation’s defense – as well as the defense of many other nations around the world.But you know all this - **and you also know that President Trump’s efforts will go nowhere unless he can prove he has overwhelming support.** The Left won’t be able to lie that the American people want this.**[And today AMAC ACTION is putting all that firepower behind President Trump’s efforts to protect our decades of hard work by asking you to help.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0M1u4yAUBeCnwTtb-MLAsGDhUeJppbqtoqhdohvACSr-ESbuz9NXrtoX6PrqHn3nPHemwxDDeL7HweuUe5MWk7yNGIb36ZoyvrkpRkyLAQqipKoEYdDmsHrDsXDaWYe1LbyupaKcK-CyuGjOLHeCKea2e-9ZLx0CZdKikjW4IugtjyoQtaKUi4ox3p-ckL2Ukip0hFOMPuUq-fl6isHimHF56adkfWWnoYj6kvO8ENYQaAm0OKDdYNNYJb-ulZ0ItDOyv_DhQfE_DChQ5JQR1l7zYCwOM4bzSNjum8LNv91_03TN0Rz2T2bfNbd3Zt_dPJSPTXk4tgTE9pgtYbvDsS1_GhRJu_k1xBgWIQmn5wFD_DLmX0y6avgMAAD__wcygQo)** My fellow patriot, my name is Rebecca Weber and I'm the Chairwoman of AMAC Action."AMAC" stands for Association of Mature American Citizens.**We exist to give Americans like YOU a voice in Washington.** With its 2 million members, AMAC is the conservative antidote to left-leaning AARP. And our 73 chapters and 330 volunteer delegates make AMAC's advocacy group, AMAC Action, a force to be reckoned with on Capitol Hill.And unlike the AARP, we’re fighting against radical democrat ideology, not alongside them. **[That’s why I’m asking you to send your tax-deductible gift to AMAC Action today.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0M1u4yAUBeCnwTtb-MLAsGDhUeJppbqtoqhdohvACSr-ESbuz9NXrtoX6PrqHn3nPHemwxDDeL7HweuUe5MWk7yNGIb36ZoyvrkpRkyLAQqipKoEYdDmsHrDsXDaWYe1LbyupaKcK-CyuGjOLHeCKea2e-9ZLx0CZdKikjW4IugtjyoQtaKUi4ox3p-ckL2Ukip0hFOMPuUq-fl6isHimHF56adkfWWnoYj6kvO8ENYQaAm0OKDdYNNYJb-ulZ0ItDOyv_DhQfE_DChQ5JQR1l7zYCwOM4bzSNjum8LNv91_03TN0Rz2T2bfNbd3Zt_dPJSPTXk4tgTE9pgtYbvDsS1_GhRJu_k1xBgWIQmn5wFD_DLmX0y6avgMAAD__wcygQo)****Your $25, $35, $50, or $100 gift gives us the resources to fight for the people who spent a lifetime working, saving, paying taxes, raising families, and playing by the rules.****People like YOU.** If you agree that America's immigration system should emphasize self-reliance and protect taxpayers, **I need you standing behind AMAC Action today.** **[Because Trump needs to hear that the Americans who actually paid the bills stand behind him.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0M1u4yAUBeCnwTtb-MLAsGDhUeJppbqtoqhdohvACSr-ESbuz9NXrtoX6PrqHn3nPHemwxDDeL7HweuUe5MWk7yNGIb36ZoyvrkpRkyLAQqipKoEYdDmsHrDsXDaWYe1LbyupaKcK-CyuGjOLHeCKea2e-9ZLx0CZdKikjW4IugtjyoQtaKUi4ox3p-ckL2Ukip0hFOMPuUq-fl6isHimHF56adkfWWnoYj6kvO8ENYQaAm0OKDdYNNYJb-ulZ0ItDOyv_DhQfE_DChQ5JQR1l7zYCwOM4bzSNjum8LNv91_03TN0Rz2T2bfNbd3Zt_dPJSPTXk4tgTE9pgtYbvDsS1_GhRJu_k1xBgWIQmn5wFD_DLmX0y6avgMAAD__wcygQo)** Thank you in advance for joining the fight to protect your hard work, Social Security, and American families.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140036331/649312225/1425818251?sourceid=1060205&refcode=WUEFEU76_20260926_EOQFourReps_PL&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZTEyNzY3YS1kY2I5LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=IAI7iPAb1FxhjpaBy8DZQPA0rBo7AL6LTwMb4LQ7yMw=) We want to be crystal clear with you, Peter: **The path to a Democratic U.S. House majority runs through EMILYs List women.** Our candidates are leaders with records of service in their communities — and they’re running in some of the most consequential House races on the map this November. But don’t just take our word for it. Hear directly from four EMILYs List women running to flip competitive seats: **1. Cait Conley — New York’s 17th Congressional District**
“When I joined the Army, I took an oath: to put service to my country above all else. And that’s what I’ve always done — throughout my six deployments, and now as I’m running for Congress.” **2. Rebecca Bennett — New Jersey’s 7th Congressional District**
“I’m running to fight for lower costs — not be a rubber stamp for reckless wars that are making life more expensive.” **3. Paige Cognetti — Pennsylvania’s 8th Congressional District**
“As Mayor, I took on the powerful, won as an independent, and put families first. In Washington, I’ll take on corruption wherever I see it and stand up for what’s best for our community.” **4. Pia Dandiya — Florida’s 22nd Congressional District**
“My parents taught me to leave the world better than I found it. That lesson took me into the classroom as a teacher and principal, serving students others had written off, and now to fighting for working families.” These four candidates are running in competitive races that could determine who controls the House next year. | | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001GY1wGv0aIAC4VTH7paqWDMwbdVMWQYTCaO4ByTe9nDBrt1b_s0TvQRGMLTRuPW1Qg6mmARqtTPvw00eUC3VvVstb8Erp5i85TW-PWDU_XKeKyTy9G2UdxbINqM6scwnQvP3j_ow435_FodCPqbbcNy0NiysV87-job904Or9UR3F1cIAVfvTCzq6V5DhFPKHb42O261eo7j8IAx-_6URRdPSSV6f08QqALTU2jbIN38=&c=Z7W23OASj7x-Ns0wNahXwfcXTjIi9pEYOaQif6CYv6V6lEJndA-tcw==&ch=OeaMdfSky9eFRDYxjYrqr_wkvKH6z6phQLDpNyNx42ias_ND4Wz8Jw==)
